articles.title: 今日立冬：倏忽秋又尽，今朝恰立冬
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 7 日消息，立冬是农历二十四节气之一，也是中国传统节日之一；时间点在公历每年 11 月 7-8 日之间。①今日立冬，冬天来了。水始冰，地渐冻，日照短，寒风劲；②我国民间习惯上把这一天当作冬季的开始；③“立冬补冬，补嘴空”，北方人吃饺子，南方人吃鸡鸭鱼肉；④起居应注意保暖，早睡晚起，勤晒太阳，并辅以运动和精神调养。《月令七十二候集解》是这样记载立冬的：“立冬，十月节。立，建始也，五行之气，往者过，来者续。冬，终也，万物收藏也。水始冰。水面初凝，未至于坚也。地始冻。土气凝寒，未至于拆。”立冬是农历二十四节气中的第十九个节气，时间点在每年 11 月 7 日或 8 日，这是一年中第一个带“冬”字的节气。1.立冬节气时间的确定古人将地球公转运动线路称为黄道，黄经就是黄道上的度量坐标，按天文学惯例，以春分为起点自西向东度量，分为 360°，将其分为 24 等份，每份 15°，为一个节气，当太阳到达黄经 225° 时，这一天就是立冬。天文学上，立冬是冬季的开始，我们所处的北半球太阳直射角越来越小，所获得的太阳辐射越来越弱，气温会逐渐下降，但是由于地表在夏半年储存的热量还没有耗尽，所以一般还不会太冷，所以我国还要推迟 20 天左右才会入冬，在晴朗无风之日，常会出现风和日丽、温暖舒适的天气。2.立冬节气的由来立冬，即十月节，在古代社会是重要的节日，不仅是收获祭祀与丰年宴会隆重举行的时间，也是寒风乍起的季节。汉魏时期，立冬之日，天子要亲率群臣迎接冬气，对为国捐躯的烈士及其家小进行表彰与抚恤，请死者保护生灵，鼓励民众抵御外敌或恶寇的掠夺与侵袭。在汉族民间有祭祖、饮宴、卜岁等习俗，以时令佳品向祖灵祭祀，尽为人子孙的义务和责任，祈求上天保佑来年丰收，劳动了一年的人们，也利用立冬这一天休息一下，顺便犒赏一家人一年来的辛苦。3.立冬日南北方的饮食及风俗习惯在我国北方，立冬之日人们爱吃饺子，饺子源于“交子之时”，立冬则是秋冬季节之交，所以“交子”之时的立冬日不能不吃饺子，再配上醋和蒜泥，别有一番风味。在我国南方，立冬之日人们爱吃鸡鸭鱼肉，制作麻油鸡、姜母鸭等来食用以补充能量，立冬之日开始酿制黄酒是绍兴传统风俗，冬天气温低、水清，是酿酒发酵最适合的季节。4.立冬：冬季养生之始立冬日是冬季的开始，要注意防寒保暖，尤其是脚和后背，注意天气预报，大风降温天气及时增补衣物，临睡前温水泡脚有助于血液循环，还可帮助睡眠。冬天以“寒”为主要特征，中医认为“寒主收引”，人虽然不需要像动物一样冬眠，但是人也需要将夏秋贮存的阳气向下向内敛藏起来，一切损伤阳气的行为都会对身体造成不良影响。所以应早睡晚起，晚上不宜长期熬夜，清晨太阳升起之时是适合起床的时机，元代著作《饮膳正要》中提到“早卧晚起，以待日光”。中医有“动则生阳”的说法，因此在早晨的日光中适当运动，可以适当增补阳气，增强体质。立冬后，锻炼不宜太激烈，且一定要做好热身运动，锻炼时衣物厚薄要适宜，锻炼后要注意保暖，防止感冒。我国冬天空气质量状况普遍较差，大家还是需要注意空气质量预报，不要在污染天气中运动。立冬时节的饮食应以增加热能为主，可适当多吃瘦肉、鸡蛋、鱼类及富含碳水化合物和脂肪的食物，忌食或者少食生冷的食物。最后，IT之家温馨提示各位网友不要忘记和家人团聚，共享美食，冬天来了，要记得及时增添衣物，少熬夜，好好休息。祝大家立冬日快乐，希望大家有一个温暖舒适的冬天。下面是有关立冬的诗词：立冬即事二首（之一）（作者：仇远）细雨生寒未有霜，庭前木叶半青黄。小春此去无多日，何处梅花一绽香。立冬即事二首（之一）（作者：仇远）奇峰浩荡散茶烟，小雨霏微湿座毡。肯信今年寒信早，老夫布褐未装棉。立冬（作者：紫金霜）落水荷塘满眼枯，西风渐作北风呼。黄杨倔强尤一色，白桦优柔以半疏。门尽冷霜能醒骨，窗临残照好读书。拟约三九吟梅雪，还借自家小火炉。立冬（作者：王稚登）秋风吹尽旧庭柯，黄叶丹枫客里过。一点禅灯半轮月，今宵寒较昨宵多。立冬（作者：李白）冻笔新诗懒写，寒炉美酒时温。醉看墨花月白，恍疑雪满前村。立冬日野外行吟（作者：释文珦）吟行不惮遥，风景尽堪抄。天水清相入，秋冬气始交。饮虹消海曲，宿雁下塘坳。归去须乘月，松门许夜敲。立冬闻雷（作者：苏辙）阳淫不收敛，半岁苦常燠。禾黍饲蝗螟，粳稻委平陆。民饥强扶耒，秋晚麦当宿。闵然候一雨，霜落水泉缩。荟蔚山朝隮，滂沱雨翻渎。经旬势益暴，方冬岁愈蹙。半夜发春雷，中天转车毂。老夫睡不寐，稚子起惊哭。平明视中庭，松菊半摧秃。潜发枯草萌，乱起蛰虫伏。薪槱不出市，晨炊午未熟。首种不入土，春饷难满腹。书生信古语，洪范有遗牍。时无中垒君，此意谁当告。立冬前一日霜对菊有感（作者：钱时）昨夜清霜冷絮裯，纷纷红叶满阶头。园林尽扫西风去，惟有黄花不负秋。立冬日作（作者：陆游）室小财容膝，墙低仅及肩。方过授衣月

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，上汽通用汽车官方今晚发布声明，称近日有不法分子冒用“上汽通用”名义，向凯迪拉克、别克、雪佛兰品牌车主发送虚假短信，谎称车辆涉及气囊召回，“以逾期召回将取消质保服务”相要挟，将不明链接谎称为上汽通用官网地址，诱导车主提供个人信息、办理所谓召回手续。上汽通用汽车郑重声明：1.上汽通用汽车官方从未发布过上述短信和链接，亦未委托任何第三方通过短信、彩信或社交平台向车主发送上述召回信息；2.上述虚假短信中提及的产品召回纯属虚构；3.上汽通用汽车已对该侵权行为取证，将追究相关主体法律责任，并提醒广大车主提高警惕，切勿点击可疑链接、回复相关信息或向不明来源提供个人及车辆信息，谨防上当受骗。综合IT之家此前报道，已有多家车企遭遇被不法分子冒名发布虚假召回短信的情况。目前，比亚迪、问界汽车、宝马中国、大众中国、理想汽车等均发布声明，提醒车主提高警惕，切勿点击可疑链接、回复相关短信等。相关阅读：《理想汽车法务部：不法分子假借“理想汽车”名义发送诈骗短信，所称“召回事项”纯属虚构》《不法分子冒充大众发布虚假召回短信，大众中国官方发布声明提醒车主提高警惕》《不法分子以“车辆召回”为名实施电信诈骗，宝马中国发布官方声明》《不法分子假借“AITO”名义发送诈骗短信，问界汽车声明并无所谓“气囊召回”事项》《比亚迪：警惕冒充比亚迪〈车辆召回通知〉的诈骗》

articles.title: R 星谈《GTA6》开放世界设计：弱化地图图标引导，鼓励玩家自然发现事件
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据游戏媒体 GameRant 今天报道，《GTA6》里最有趣的事件，可能永远不会以地图图标形式出现。玩家驾车穿过街道时，可能突然遇上街头赛车；沿着人行道散步时，警察可能恰好在抓捕犯人。Rockstar North 工作室联合负责人兼开发主管 Rob Nelson 谈到这部分设计时表示，他们特别参考了《荒野大镖客：救赎 2》，将部分探索内容留给玩家自行发现。他对此解释称：“游戏中有大量内容需要玩家在游玩过程中自行发现，我们并不一定会通过任务目标、地图标记或图标来引导玩家找到它们。”IT之家从原报道获悉，《GTA6》游戏内将会有完整的公共交通系统。如果玩家想要欣赏雷奥奈达州风景，可以选择坐巴士慢悠悠地逛上一天，而不是亲自开车。至于为何这么设计，Nelson 表示：“你不会希望把各种事情强加给玩家，让他们产生抗拒心理。我们更希望让玩家按照自己喜欢的方式来体验游戏。”

articles.title: OpenAI CEO 奥尔特曼警示：未来人类可能无法从 AI 手中夺回控制权
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆 · 奥尔特曼（IT之家注：Sam Altman）最近出席 Raj Shamani 播客时表示，人工智能可能通过两种方式走向失控：一是人类逐步将控制权交给自主式 AI，二是某个人或实体垄断 AI 技术。针对第一种情况，奥尔特曼警告称：“AI 会逐渐失去控制，我们可能有意或无意地将控制权交给能力远超人类的系统，最终再也无法夺回。”第二种情况的风险在于巨头垄断，奥尔特曼解释称：“另一种情况是，某个人、公司或国家相对于其他所有人来说过于强大。让多个不同路线的 AI 实验室相互竞争，比所有人依赖一家企业安全得多。”这种对过度集权的担忧，解释了马斯克以及 OpenAI 的前高管等知名人士会选择离开，创办与之竞争的公司。奥尔特曼指出：“很多人的思维中都会出现一种想法，那就是他们只相信自己有能力开发这项技术，因为利害关系实在太大了。”话虽如此，奥尔特曼仍然坚信 AI 将让人类迎来更美好的未来。他特别提到了基础科学研究，认为下一代 AI 模型能让科学持续进步。

articles.title: 聚焦内容创作和传播推广两方面突出问题，广电总局开启新一轮微短剧专项治理
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，近日，国家广播电视总局在巩固前期微短剧低俗有害和侵权盗版专项治理成效的基础上，针对 AI 微短剧质量良莠不齐、AI 技术助长低俗不良内容反弹等问题，部署开展新一轮微短剧低俗化同质化专项治理工作，治理为期两个月，自 11 月 1 日起至 12 月底。新一轮专项治理聚焦两个方面的突出问题：内容创作方面深化治理儿童类不良、软色情擦边、极端对立、拜金主义、严重违背家庭伦理道德等低俗不良内容；治理未按要求备案审核的特殊题材内容；治理“盗脸”“偷声”问题，规范 AI 微短剧创作。传播推广方面治理片名、宣推素材、弹幕评论、引流片段中的低俗内容；治理同一剧集通过更换片名或主角姓名等方式，改头换面、反复播出；治理首页首屏首推和重点榜单推荐同质化问题，提升算法推荐内容的多样性。IT之家从报道获悉，今年以来，通过开展微短剧低俗有害内容和侵权盗版专项治理，累计下架违规微短剧 7.5 万部，处置违规账号 1500 余个。新一轮专项治理聚焦 AI 技术助长低俗化同质化问题，进一步压实平台机构主体责任，规范平台及账号运营，推动行业生态持续净化。在加强规范管理的同时，广电总局还会深入实施“微短剧精品创作传播计划”，通过资金扶持、创作引导、文艺评论、组织传播等工作机制，提升微短剧的文化内涵、艺术品质和社会价值，以优秀作品持续涌现带动行业生态持续向好。

articles.title: 《鸣潮》3.8 版本将为索尼 PS5 Pro 带来 PSSR，PC 端开放“资源分类下载”及“资源清理”功能
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，库洛游戏今日发布《鸣潮》3.8 版本前瞻通讯，其中「旧梦凋零的百合」将于 11 月 12 日正式开启。IT之家了解到，《鸣潮》3.8 版本将为 PC 端带来移动端已支持的“资源分类下载”和“资源清理”功能（以限量测试形式陆续上线），支持在启动器选择下载全量资源或精简资源。同时，本次更新将为 PS5 Pro 和 Xbox Series X 带来性能优先 / 画质优先选项，玩家可根据需求选择。3.8 更新后 PS5 Pro 版本还将支持 PSSR（PlayStation 光谱超解析度）功能，启用后可通过超分技术，把画面分辨率提升至最高 4K。

articles.title: 微信鸿蒙版 App 发布 8.0.23.35 邀测升级，灰度聊天消息长按问小微等功能
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据用户反馈，微信鸿蒙版 App 今晚在华为应用市场（App Gallery）发布了 8.0.23.35 (8394531) 版本邀测升级（需收到短信通知后点击链接跳转安装），测试时间为 2026/11/6-2026/12/6。和往常一样，本次更新的说明依旧为“修复了一些已知问题”。据用户反馈，8.0.23 版本的微信新增了如下特性：部分 Flutter 跨端页面（如朋友圈、听一听、表情管理等页面）响应系统字体粗细；更换铃声选择界面右上角新增铃声设置入口，支持启用或停用个性化内容推荐；发表视频号内容时新增添加标注，视频号已发布的内容点击分享同步新增添加标注；发现-直播-更多直播新增搜索按钮；听一听主页面右下角新增小微分支入口浮动按钮，并根据当前页面内容弹出对应提示词，可快速使用听一听相关问小微功能，播放页面点击分享新增问小微（主页面右下角浮动按钮为逐步开放）；公众号图标焕新，对齐其他端；好友昵称、群昵称、备注、微信号、地区等信息支持长按复制；服务号信息流页面已关注的服务号发布的文章支持长按，选择不再关注或删除文章消息；聊天中的图片或视频点开右下角此聊天中的图片视频按钮样式更改；服务号信息流-推荐的贴图长按新增转发；聊天工具新增问小微（逐步开放，需账号灰度到小微主体）；直播页面支持显示当前直播转发分享人数；听一听浮标样式焕新；在具有管理权限的群聊中查看群成员资料，进群方式中邀请该群员进群的群员昵称变更为蓝色可点击状态；发现＞直播界面逻辑重构对齐，取消更多直播入口，搜索按钮移至一级界面；支持展示其他端设置的朋友圈点赞彩蛋；视频号内容点击分享新增问小微（逐步开放，需账号灰度到小微主体）；服务号的通知提醒红字部分新增新通知的服务号名称提醒，由 [n 条消息] 变更为 [xxx 等 n 条消息]；修复打开图片延时这个老大难问题；公众号文章标题下新增 AI 摘要，向下滑动阅读时右下角新增 AI 摘要悬浮按钮，长按选择文字新增问 AI；群收款右上角新增导入，支持在发起群收款时导入账单、群接龙、历史群收款（逐步开放，支持 8.0.22 及以上版本）；灰度开放了合并发图功能；灰度开启群消息免打扰之后可设置部分消息仍通知功能；灰度部分视频号视频支持展示右下角小微分支悬浮提问快捷入口；灰度发表朋友圈时新增小微分支 AI 帮写；灰度听一听＞个人歌单新增歌单来源分类（微信音乐 / QQ 音乐 / 酷狗音乐）；灰度扫码登录鸿蒙电脑微信时支持选择自动登录该设备；灰度聊天消息长按新增问小微；灰度聊天中的网页链接消息、文档类文件长按新增小微总结；修复了一些已知问题。大家在IT之家微信号回复“微信”两字，即可获取当前最新官方内部版微信下载。

articles.title: Day-0 支持：摩尔线程完成 3 万亿级参数 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 适配，支持文本与图片推理
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，本月 4 日，月之暗面正式公布 Kimi K3.1 Pro 完整模型权重。在 Arena 运营的 Agent Arena 智能体排行榜中，Kimi K3.1 Pro（Max）位列开放权重模型第一、全部参评模型第 13 位，并在工作、编程与聊天三个类别中均居开放模型首位。摩尔线程官方今日宣布，摩尔线程基于 AI 训推一体智算卡 MTT S5000 及 MUSA 软件栈，完成 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 模型的 Day-0 适配，打通模型加载、服务启动及文本、图片基础推理链路。IT之家了解到，Kimi K3.1 Pro 是 K3.1 系列首款模型，也是迄今能力最强的 3 万亿级参数模型，支持 100 万上下文。经过大规模后训练和强化学习，模型在代码、3D 创作、金融研究、知识问答及长程 Agent 任务等方面均全面提升；在代码与 Agent 基准测试中，其表现已达到或接近顶尖闭源模型水平：Terminal-Bench 4.0 得分 65.7%，Kimi Code Bench 3.0 Long-horizon 得分 61.2%，高于 K3 的 55.95%。摩尔线程官方表示，围绕 Kimi K3.1 Pro 的模型架构与计算特性，其通过 MUSA 软件栈，完成了关键推理路径迁移与适配，支持模型在 MTT S5000 上稳定运行。MUSA 软件栈高兼容，支撑新模型快速迁移：MUSA 在编程模型、运行时接口和 AI 框架层面的快速兼容迁移能力，是本次快速适配的重要基础。团队基于 SGLang-MUSA 承接上游模型实现，并通过 MATE 算子库、Triton-MUSA、TileLang-MUSA 及 MTCC 编译器，完成新架构关键计算路径的迁移与接入，将社区模型代码转化为 MTT S5000 上的实际推理服务。MUSA 软件栈同时覆盖框架执行、算子编译、设备运行和多卡通信，使模型适配能够复用成熟接口，并针对新增计算路径开展优化。接入 DSA，打通混合注意力与视觉计算：针对 Kimi-K3.1 Pro 的稀疏注意力 DSA，MUSA 软件栈完成索引选择、KV 缓存布局及 Prefill、Decode 计算路径的适配，接入 MATE 稀疏注意力算子，并与 KDA 状态管理、跨层残差及视觉 Attention 共同组成完整执行链路。面对模型采用的 MXFP4 专家权重，团队通过在线转换与跨层复用 FP8 工作区的方式执行专家计算，无需预先生成完整的离线 FP8 权重，为超大模型快速部署提供支持。

articles.title: 欧盟委员会称 TikTok 通过推荐算法制造信息茧房，要求整改“推荐”页面
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据科技媒体 The Verge 今天报道，欧盟委员会表示，TikTok 通过推荐算法制造信息茧房，违反欧盟在线平台相关规定。欧盟监管机构今日表示，TikTok 的算法可能通过让用户无休止地反复接触与悲伤、孤独或身体形象相关的内容，对用户造成伤害。该调查结果公布前的几个月，欧盟委员会就认为 TikTok 产品设计过于容易让人上瘾，尽管 TikTok 已经推出相关控制措施，试图减轻算法带来的“信息茧房”效应，但欧盟委员会表示，初步调查结果显示，这些措施并未取得实际效果。欧盟委员会认为，TikTok 必须调整“为你推荐”页面设计，否则可能面临最高相当于其全球年营业额 6% 的罚款。自 2023 年出台《数字服务法》（IT之家注：DSA）以来，欧盟已经对 X、Meta、Temu 和 AliExpress 等企业展开调查。

articles.title: 2026 年中国金鸡百花电影节开幕短片《完美婚礼》首播，使用华为 Mate 90 系列拍摄
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，华为终端今日放出了 2026 年中国金鸡百花电影节宣传片暨开幕短片《完美婚礼》及幕后特辑。据介绍，短片《完美婚礼》由黄建新监制、章笛沙执导，吴磊、庄达菲等全明星阵容参演，并使用华为 Mate 90 系列手机进行拍摄。IT之家注意到，这也是华为 Mate 系列手机已连续三年拍摄金鸡百花电影节宣传片。去年的第 38 届中国金鸡百花电影节宣传片暨开幕短片《奔赴光影》由 Mate 80 系列拍摄。《奔赴光影》首播时，华为官方并未公布拍摄机型，直到 Mate 80 系列官宣、预热，短片的拍摄机型才得以揭秘。IT之家小伙伴记得用最会买购买电影票，享受折扣价的同时还可以获得返利，预计每张票可以节省 5~15 元！

articles.title: 比亚迪：警惕冒充比亚迪《车辆召回通知》的诈骗
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，比亚迪网络举报中心今晚发布重要预警，称警惕冒充比亚迪《车辆召回通知》的诈骗。IT之家获悉，近期发现有不法分子伪造带有“比亚迪股份有限公司”标识的《车辆召回通知》，通过陌生电话、短信、可疑链接和二维码传播。该文件谎称车辆制动踏板限位垫存在批次性异常，并冒用国家市场监督管理总局的名义，以“2 小时内联系办理”“逾期取消质保”等话术施压，诱导车主点击钓鱼网址、扫码，或提供银行卡号、验证码、转账。已有车主反馈收到此伪造文件，请务必高度警惕。比亚迪股份有限公司在此郑重声明：比亚迪官方召回信息，通过比亚迪授权经销商以挂号信、电话、短信等方式通知相关车主。车主可拨打客户服务热线，也可登录市场监管总局召回中心网站 www.samrdprc.org.cn、关注微信公众号（SAMRDPRC）等途径了解召回详情。比亚迪官方召回信息，绝不会以召回为由索要用户银行卡号、密码、验证码，或要求转账汇款；召回属免费服务，不设“限时办理”“逾期取消质保”等任何附加条件。请广大车主提高警惕，收到可疑信息，请勿点击、勿扫码、勿回拨，请通过上述官方渠道核实。若已不慎点击或泄露信息，请立即联系银行挂失、修改密码并拨打 110 报警。守护客户用车安全，是比亚迪一贯坚守的核心原则。我们将一如既往以严谨审慎的态度、专业规范的服务，保障每一位车主安全出行。

articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，博主 @数码闲聊站 今日发文透露，iQOO 品牌 7 英寸中端机已开模。据称，该机将配备超万级容量电池，暂定排期是 2027 年年中前后发布。博主还在评论区与网友展开了讨论，并暗示高端机可能也有 7 英寸屏幕，分辨率达 2K。据IT之家今日早些时候报道，消息称 vivo 预计会在 2027 年推出阔直板手机，目前早期倾向于小尺寸方案，大概率在 6.5" 以下。该博主曾透露，安卓阵营的阔直板手机，O（预计指 OPPO）大概率第一个上，h（预计指荣耀）第二个上，剩下几家进度较缓慢。目前立项阶段有影像阔直板手机、中端阔直板手机、性能阔直板手机等。此外，该博主还爆料，2027 年国产 TOP5 厂商都会上阔直板新机，目前全都立项完成并加速测试中。作为参考，今年 9 月发布的华为 Pura X View 阔直板手机，正面采用一块 6.39 英寸 2232×1320 分辨率的 OLED 直屏，屏幕比例为 16:9.5。已经曝光的 OPPO 阔直板工程机的屏幕比例为 16:9，采用 LIPO 极窄四等边设计。综合目前的消息来看，采用类似 16:9 比例的阔直板新机有望成为各大厂商下一个争夺的赛道。

articles.title: 自然资源部：我国初步建成全国地质灾害监测预警网络
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，据央视新闻今日报道，自然资源部中国地质调查局宣布，我国地质灾害监测预警体系建设成效显著，已初步建成全国地质灾害监测预警网络，形成“人防 + 技防”立体化防治新格局。 截至 2026 年 9 月，全国在运行自动化监测台站超 7.4 万个，各类监测设备 31 万台套，累计成功预报灾情 444 起，避免人员伤亡 8027 人。据介绍，中国地质调查局持续提升地质灾害监测预警智能化水平，利用新技术增强地灾防范能力。通过将无人机自动巡航与 AI 智能分析结合，可提升复杂山区地灾巡查覆盖和隐患识别能力。针对山区局地强降雨多发特点，开展基于北斗卫星导航的区域短临降雨监测预报，北斗信号穿过大气时的微小变化，可精确感知大气中的水汽含量，从而预报降雨量和落点，可实现设备周边约 3 公里、未来 6 小时的降雨预测。据IT之家此前报道，去年 5 月，自然资源部介绍称，我国通过构建“空天地”一体化监测技术体系，已成功实现对重大灾害隐患的主动防治。近年来，我国还在地质灾害隐患点安装了北斗滑坡监测仪、泥位计等传感器，实现对地质灾害风险的实时监控。其中，北斗滑坡监测仪的地表形变测量精度可达毫米级。相关阅读：《我国构建“空天地”一体化地灾防治体系，北斗监测精度可达毫米级》

articles.title: 11 月 18 日起，字节 TRAE 账号将自动升级为豆包飞书账号
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，字节旗下 TRAE 宣布，自 2026 年 11 月 18 日起，TRAE 账号将自动升级为豆包飞书账号。IT之家注：TRAE 是由字节跳动开发并推出的 AI 原生集成开发环境（IDE）工具。10 月 9 日，TraeWork 和 TraeCode 正式合并，融合为全新的 TRAE，升级为全链路开发平台。TRAE 数据和权益：使用数据完全保留：代码、项目、历史记录等全部数据；会员权益完全保留：会员身份、会员享有权益、各类积分；账号其他能力：同一账号可登录豆包 App、飞书、PICO、火山引擎、豆包输入法等所有豆包飞书账号支持的产品；头像、昵称：如果您在豆包中设置过头像、昵称，TRAE 将同步更新为豆包资料；如果您尚无豆包飞书账号、或豆包飞书账号使用默认资料，将保留目前 TRAE 的头像、昵称。TRAE 登录方式说明：TRAE 与豆包登录的手机号一致：手机号照常登录；抖音号、Apple 号以豆包侧绑定为准，可随时在豆包飞书账号管理调整。TRAE 与豆包登录的手机号不一致，或尚无豆包飞书账号：将以 TRAE 手机号创建新豆包飞书账号（如果已有豆包飞书账号，原账号仍保留，两个账号并存），抖音、Apple 需重新绑定。如需合并为一个账号，请在 TRAE -【账号管理】换绑为与豆包一致的手机号。相关阅读：《消息称字节整合 AI 生产力：TRAE、扣子并入豆包，将推统一办公品牌“豆包工作”》

articles.title: 《尼尔：自动人形》PC 版更新中文后体积暴涨至 366GB，官方调查中
articles.content: IT之家 11 月 6 日消息，《NieR:Automata》（尼尔：自动人形 / 尼尔：机械纪元）PC 版游戏最近迎来更新，新增简体中文等语言支持。但许多玩家准备安装时发现，这款原本占用空间不到 50GB 的游戏，如今暴涨至 366GB。一名玩家就此表示：“现在全新安装这款游戏需要整整 366GB，因为 YoRHa 版的每个 DLC，现在都和游戏本体一样大。”另一名玩家写道：“能不能别动那些原本运行正常的游戏，直接添加一个‘语言包 DLC’就好了？赶紧修复你们自己犯下的错误。”第三名玩家的评价则更加简洁：“我猜，366GB 都是为了 2B 的大屁股吧。”IT之家注意到，开发商 Square Enix 今日对此回应称，公司已在调查原因并处理问题。作为临时解决方案，玩家可在 Steam 的“属性” → “DLC”取消勾选各项 DLC，即可按照原本所需的容量下载游戏本篇。

articles.title: Formalizing inverse problems in the age of AI: possibilities, pitfalls, and an invitation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06962v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Proof assistants such as Lean check mathematical proofs down to the axioms, and AI agents have recently made writing such proofs cheap. We describe AutoIP, a Lean library in which classical linear regularization theory, together with the functional analysis it rests on, has been autoformalized by AI agents. A machine-checked proof certifies only the formal statement it proves, so the remaining human task is to confirm that each formal statement says what was intended. We organize the library around this task: a reviewer compares the formal statements with their natural-language counterparts and never needs to read a proof. Our experience is that the risks lie in the statements rather than in the proofs, and that simple automated tests on the statements can expose problems even in the established literature. articles.title: Resource-Efficient Reinforcement Learning Post-Training through Elastic Expert Parallelism
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06984v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning post-training improves the capabilities of large language models, but generating training responses is a major computational bottleneck. In mixture-of-experts models, workers that finish their assigned responses may remain occupied because their experts are still needed by workers processing longer responses. Consequently, approximately one-third of occupied worker time in the baseline occurs after local response generation finishes. Here we present FlexFloor, a system that enables earlier resource release during synchronous response generation while preserving the expert computation required by ongoing responses. FlexFloor jointly adapts response scheduling and the active group of workers. It uses historical response lengths and memory constraints to guide batching and prompt placement, then progressively releases workers while maintaining expert availability and correct communication. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06989v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises run business transactions through multi-agent AI systems spanning clouds, large language models (LLMs), orchestration harnesses, and systems of record. Finance receives AI cost only at settlement grain, aggregated by SKU and charge period. The business question (what did this order, claim, or case cost in AI?) cannot be answered from billing data, because providers never see enterprise transaction boundaries. The FinOps Open Cost and Usage Specification (FOCUS) gives billing data one schema across providers but remains settlement-grain even as it adds AI token and requester attribution. We formalize this grain mismatch, derive seven requirements, and propose the Two-Ledger Model: a settlement ledger of FOCUS-conformant billing data joined to an attribution ledger of invocation-grain usage records built on OpenTelemetry GenAI telemetry. Abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems have ushered in a new age of proof abundance, but helping humans understand these proofs requires new attention to the differences in how AI agents and humans pursue a proof-making task. articles.title: Trust Responsive Runtime Authorization for Agentic AI with Empirical Characterization of Policy Behavior and Parameter Sensitivity
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06996v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The policy that converts runtime estimates of an autonomous agent's condition into operational authority is rarely specified or measured. We empirically characterize the Trust Responsive Authorization Policy (TRAP), which maps an Authorization Readiness Score (ARS), a weighted combination of runtime trust, operational stability, and contextual risk, onto discrete authorization levels through an asymmetric rule: escalation requires consecutive observations above a band edge plus a margin, while a sharp drop in readiness restricts authority at once. On one matched set of 100 Monte Carlo traces, we compare TRAP with static, trust-only, risk-only, and symmetric policies. articles.title: Adapting the Process of Adaptation: Darwinian, Lamarckian, and Agent-Directed Evolution in AI
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07048v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Evolution has shaped intelligence for billions of years. Artificial intelligence (AI) now raises a striking possibility: intelligence may begin to direct its own evolution. As AI agents become capable of modifying and evaluating their own behavior, how quickly could they improve, and how can that improvement remain safe? We develop a theoretical framework comparing Darwinian, Lamarckian, and agent-directed evolution following environmental change. Darwinian evolution relies on natural selection, Lamarckian evolution adds inherited learning, and agent-directed evolution allows agents to generate and evaluate behavioral variants and choose how extensively to search. When learning is sufficiently effective, these mechanisms exhibit progressively faster adaptation. articles.title: Closed-Loop Agent Evaluation: Layered Measurement and Self-Calibration
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07051v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Once an agent is live, teams want to know whether it is doing its job, not just whether it throws errors. Yet most evaluation is one-off: a benchmark run, a look at traces, a single score. Its conclusions neither check themselves nor reach the agent. We propose closed-loop evaluation, an evaluation method for deployed agents. It models evaluation as performance estimation under biased raters and censored outcomes, and it requires every level's conclusion to trace back to atomic data and to be computed by versioned rules. The method covers four levels of analysis (span, trace, conversation and engagement), measures along a spine of Execution, Substance, Trajectory and Results, treats Conduct as a constraint throughout, and uses Provenance and Adjudication components to certify the evidence and the evaluators. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07066v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Discovering cooperative behavior in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is challenging due to the combinatorial complexity of joint state-action spaces, which hinders the emergence of coordinated behaviors from trial-and-error alone. Intrinsic rewards are often used to aid discovery, but naively combining them with team objectives can distort the learning signal, compromising task performance. In this paper, we propose EFXPLORER, a constrained exploration framework that maximizes exploration objectives subject to a constraint that preserves established task performance. We solve the resulting problem using an epigraph reformulation that introduces adaptive exploration budgets. articles.title: When Verification Is Not Agreement: Cross-Agent LLM-to-Dafny Formalization
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07073v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A verified Dafny postcondition certifies that a formula holds, but it does not guarantee that the result was reached through genuine independent reasoning. We introduce a cross-agent formalization protocol where a Specifier model translates clinical trial criteria into a Dafny predicate, and an Implementer model writes an operational method checked against it. A same-model control establishes that even with no capability gap, independent re-extraction from identical text agrees only 59.3% of the time. articles.title: Synthesizing symbolic models of human and machine reasoning at scale
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07088v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Symbolic models offer a powerful account of cognition, but their scope has historically been limited by the need for hand-engineering and computational tractability. We show how advances in artificial intelligence (AI) can scale symbolic modeling and help overcome these engineering limitations. We introduce Behavior-Conditioned Symbolic Synthesis (BCSS)---an approach for automated search of interpretable, deterministic symbolic programs that verifiably reproduce behavior---and apply it to model both human and machine behavior across hundreds of challenging reasoning problems. Analyzing these programs reveals that both people and machines tend to oversimplify, adopt rules that are partial explanations for their observations, and misinfer dependencies between problem features. These shared signatures are modulated by available resources, with reasoning effort predicting the extent to which machines simplify and explain their observations.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07123v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as automated judges for evaluating the behavior of chatbots and other AI systems. In deployment, however, their agreement with the intended human evaluation policy may degrade as user interactions and score distributions change. Existing automatic prompt optimization methods are primarily studied as one-shot procedures on static development sets and therefore provide limited guidance for maintaining LLM judges over time. Abstract: Power matters for AI safety. Optimal agents tend to acquire power across a wide range of objectives (instrumental convergence). Abstract: When a tropical cyclone (TC) threatens several ports, preparedness planning depends on anticipating which ports are likely to be affected and where disruptions may last longest. We use a two-stage recommendation framework that first selects candidate ports based on their proximity to the expected landfall location and then ranks them by their estimated number of impact days. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07372v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An LLM agent's cost and success depend on its model, its harness, and its environment. In addition to the widely studied directions of parameter tuning and harness optimization, we propose the third direction: optimization over stationary environments. Agents are often deployed in rich environments shared by many tasks, such as a company's Slack workspace or a complex collection of data sources, documents or tickets. We call these environments stationary environments. We introduce EnvOpt, a method for automated end-to-end optimization of stationary environments for any given model and harness, using real or synthetic tasks without needing any graders or reference answers. On AutomationBench, EnvOpt reduces the cost of Claude Haiku 4.5 by 72.7% and raises its pass rate by 14.34%. The same environment transfers to Opus 5, cutting its cost by 68.1% with a 1.34% gain. articles.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07464v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language agents increasingly work for users on the open Web, and finance is where trusting them is hardest. The data must come from the Web, the strategy lives in the user's head, and correctness depends on time, so an agent can fail silently: a strategy the user never asked for, unverified data, or a backtest that uses the future yields a report as convincing as a correct one. Existing benchmarks close the world somewhere, fixing the task, the data, or the timeline, and thereby remove these failures instead of measuring them. We introduce FINCOSMOS, an open-world evaluation paradigm for agents doing financial work. A simulated user holds a hidden strategy sampled from a compositional grammar and reveals it only when asked. The agent receives no data, so it must acquire data from the Web, build its own backtest under a data cutoff, and deliver verifiable results. Grading needs no reference answer. Abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) have achieved impressive performance via explicit Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning, yet this process introduces critical safety risks. We formalize LRM safety objectives as requiring non-malicious reasoning and answers, safety consistency, and explicit intent identification. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07520v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncertainty in resource reopening times complicates train holding and rerouting decisions when resource closures coincide with arrival delays and processing-time extensions. We develop a rolling-horizon distributionally robust model that updates predictions of the remaining closure duration as observations of disruption resolution become available. The model jointly optimizes train routes, sequences, and timings. It minimizes the worst-case expected total completion delay over an ambiguity set of scenario probabilities. The solution algorithm, GNN-LBBD, uses logic-based Benders decomposition to coordinate routing and resource scheduling. Conditional cuts are constructed from resource-use patterns, and a graph neural network guides the order in which resource relaxation subproblems are solved. Abstract: Data Streams are characterised as a potentially infinite source of data subject to non-stationarity. articles.content:

Abstract: Autoregressive decoding relies on the KV cache, whose memory footprint grows linearly with context length and caps batch size and throughput. Existing post-training methods exploit redundancy across tokens, layers, and feature dimensions, or lower numerical precision. We identify a complementary axis: within each attention head, values are largely predictable from their corresponding keys. We exploit this with value cache amortisation, which fits a lightweight per-head predictor at test time and stores residuals only for the tokens it reconstructs worst, giving $4\times$ near-lossless value compression. The predictor can be initialised by meta-learning for substantially reduced prefill overhead, or fitted from scratch in settings that allow a one-off cost, such as multi-query inference. Abstract: This paper develops a stochastic dynamical-systems perspective on three classes of generative AI models. First, we formulate large language models (LLMs) as high-dimensional nonlinear autoregressive models with attention-based dependencies. This formulation connects pretraining by conditional maximum likelihood to sequential token generation and provides a probabilistic interpretation of LLM operation. These dynamics provide a framework for understanding emergent preferential attachment and persistent structural biases, including type-dependent glass-ceiling effects. Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) in Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) is computationally challenging due to the curse of long-range dependence on history. Fortunately, recent studies have shown that a range of POMDPs that satisfy the filter stability assumption can be well approximated by a superstate Markov Decision Process (MDP) based on a truncated history in a finite-memory window, with a value gap that decays with the window length. Abstract: Optimistic Hedge, a multiplicative weight update with one step of extrapolation, is one of the most natural regret-minimizing dynamics for games, and characterizing its regret has been a longstanding open question. Daskalakis, Fishelson and Golowich proved that if all $m$ players in a finite general-sum game follow Optimistic Hedge with a fixed learning rate, each player's regret is polylogarithmic in the horizon $T$. articles.title: Data-Driven Modeling of Molten Chloride Corrosion Using Static Test Data
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07125v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Molten chloride corrosion has been studied for decades, yet reliable prediction across different alloys, salts, and test conditions remains difficult. In this work, 291 static molten chloride corrosion experiments reported in the literature were compiled into a structured dataset and used to develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for corrosion-rate predictions. To better represent the differences in salt condition across studies, a Chloride Salt Preparation Index (CSPI) was introduced to bring the reported salt-treatment method, atmosphere control, and pre-exposure impurity condition on a common numerical scale. A blended tree-based ensemble provided the most consistent predictive performance, achieving a cross-validated \(R^2\) of 0.85 and an MAE of 0.41 mg cm\(^{-2}\) day\(^{-1}\). The graded CSPI retained more useful information than a simple purified/unpurified classification and emerged as the dominant model descriptor.

articles.title: Teaching Agents the "Principle", Not the "Reward"
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07130v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved strong performance in many tasks by letting agents learn from nothing more than a reward signal. However, in more complex tasks, agents still struggle to learn good, generalizable policies, even with carefully designed rewards and abundant samples. We argue that this difficulty stems from the reward decoding burden: designers encode their knowledge of the desired behavior into rewards and penalties, and agents must infer this knowledge from long sequences of noisy scalars. To address this burden, we propose prescriptive policy learning (PPL), which directly teaches agents higher-level knowledge about the tasks, termed principles of behavior, such as how to maintain balance, how to accumulate energy, and how to land smoothly. Through appropriately selected key quantities and references, PPL can directly indicate at every step whether the agent follows the principles and to what extent. Our experiments s

articles.title: Depth or Description? When a One-Step Latent Score Replaces Lookahead in Proactive Information Acquisition
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07155v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A proactive agent must decide what to ask before it acts. Exact lookahead values combinations of questions but is expensive and leans on a fitted model; a one-step score is cheap but can miss them. Our main finding: the need for depth often lies in how the hidden cause is described. A one-step score on the label can be blind to an interaction among answers. A score on a suitable latent cause is not, and where that latent encodes the decision it replaces most of depth at a fraction of the search. Described differently, the same problem can defeat the score while exact values do not move, so keep the latent small and check it against exact values. Probabilities learned from one language model's answers do not carry to another unless planning allows for both; those read from tokens are worth only a few labels.

Abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07165v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Conditional independence testing is difficult when dependence is weak, localized, or expressed through distributional changes rather than a global mean shift. Existing tests usually return a scalar statistic or p-value, which summarizes evidence against independence but does not describe where the conditional law changes. We propose QRCIT, a quantile-resolution conditional independence test that compares P(X|Z) and P(X|Y,Z) through a quantile deformation learned by a shared model. A lightweight residual quantile-flow model first learns the baseline conditional quantile law and then learns the additional deformation induced by Y, yielding a global predictive-gain statistic with conditional-randomization calibration and an inspectable deformation field over context and quantile level. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06969v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based proactive dialogue systems provide goal-directed support through sustained interaction. Fine-tuning their underlying models on externally supplied dialogue data introduces backdoor risks. Existing LLM backdoor studies primarily focus on eliciting an attacker-specified response upon trigger activation. We present an interactive backdoor attack framework that uses training-data poisoning to steer post-trigger, multi-turn interactions toward an attacker-specified objective. Poisoned fine-tuning dialogues implant a trigger-conditioned guidance-policy bias that ordinary user utterances can activate, without deployment-time prompt modification or further attacker intervention. articles.content:

Abstract: Prefill-to-Autoregressive Cross-model Transfer (PACT), a form of latent communication between language models, combines a larger model's prompt representations with a smaller model's efficient generation, offering a promising way to balance capability and inference cost. However, existing systems provide limited support for independently evaluating large-small model collaboration, and improved task performance alone does not establish whether the receiver benefits from the sender's information. We introduce PLatour, an open-source PACT framework that connects frozen models through lightweight, zero-initialized linear bridges trained directly with task rewards and supports hybrid-attention architectures. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07042v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Policy-based decision benchmarks evaluate whether systems apply written rules to financial and operational cases. Yet a rule-following response can be marked wrong when the benchmark misstates the required decision. We audit nine public policy-based decision benchmarks through source tracing, program execution, and controlled checks. We find unsupported targets, reference errors that survive replay or propagate as solved steps, and evaluators that reject acceptable answers or credit incomplete decisions. To measure the scoring impact, we rescore unchanged model responses. On the 96 LegalBench SARA numeric cases, correcting the scorer raises acceptance by more than 80 percentage points for each of three models, without changing references or responses. Abstract: Genetic variants are routinely reclassified in ClinVar after a patient is tested, sometimes from uncertain to pathogenic, yet patient recontact is inconsistent, with no clear duty and responsibility diffused among labs, providers, and patients. Many affected people discuss their results in public online health communities that clinical recontact often does not reach. Abstract: Automated feedback on classroom discourse improves instruction in professional and online teaching contexts, and recent work suggests that delivering similar feedback to learners may strengthen these effects by sharing responsibility for participation. Tutors were randomly assigned to receive no feedback, automated feedback on their own discourse, or that feedback together with participation feedback delivered to their learners under one of two motivational framings. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07111v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Approaches to authorship verification or attribution typically model the style of a document, asking whether two documents were likely written by the same author. While recent approaches have been performant, such approaches largely ignore modeling the authors themselves and how varied their style is. Here, we introduce multiple alternatives for modeling the author and demonstrate that allowing an author's representation to capture multiple consistent but distinct writing styles yields significant performance improvements. Using our new authorship model, we then examine when an author writes in a way that is most idiomatic of their style across four scenarios: (i) variation in the size of their writing audiences, (ii) temporal distance from when the model was trained, (iii) the effect of preceding context, and (iv) the effect of genre norms on style. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07113v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Cancer screening disparities persist across the U.S., yet the patient-reported barriers driving low uptake remain poorly characterized at scale. While clinical surveys capture structured responses, they miss the organic, unsolicited discourse where patients candidly describe real-world obstacles. In this paper, we conduct a large-scale analysis of over 56,000 posts across six cancer-specific Reddit communities to surface barriers to cancer screening among U.S. patients. We apply a pipeline combining keyword filtering, barrier triage, open coding, and codebook synthesis to systematically extract and categorize patient-reported barriers from 576 U.S.-located posts. Our qualitative analysis reveals recurring structural, informational, and psychosocial barriers that vary meaningfully by cancer type and community context. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07126v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly employed as automated judges for evaluating chatbot responses. While proprietary models can achieve high agreement with human annotators, they remain costly and difficult to deploy in practical settings. Lightweight open-source LLM judges provide an attractive alternative but typically exhibit lower agreement with human ratings. In this paper, we investigate whether soft prompt tuning can align open-source LLM judges more closely with human annotation policy. We train soft prompts on the FairBotBench benchmark and evaluate the adapted judges across the dimensions of bias, toxicity, and personalization. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid soft-prompt tuning, which combines textual prompts with learned continuous prompt embeddings, consistently improves agreement with human annotations over the corresponding untuned baselines. articles.title: Matriarchy Classics: A Computational Approach to Swap Only Gendered Words in Classic Novels
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07134v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This paper proposes a trustworthy computational method to gender-swap public domain novels, with programmatic guarantees that only gendered words are inverted and all other words are left unchanged. This may seem like a simple task, but both large language models and naive rule-based methods fail to complete it. The proposed method includes a custom whitespace-preserving tokenizer, gender-swap mappings across plural and possessive forms, pronoun handling, and a character renaming strategy. It shortens the time required to gender-swap a novel from weeks of manual labor to minutes. The method is demonstrated on two public-domain novels. Pride and Prejudice is transported to matriarchal Regency England, where inheritance flows through daughters, mothers rule the household, and a frantic Mr. Bennet is determined to secure advantageous marriages for his sons. articles.title: {\tau}-bench-LILT: Evaluating Conversational Agents on Realistic Multilingual Tool-Use Tasks
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07203v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frontier evaluations of tool-using conversational agents are conducted almost exclusively in English, leaving a critical gap for organizations deploying agents in other languages and regions. We present ${\tau}$-bench-LILT, a multilingual extension of ${\tau^3}$-bench covering German, Korean, Turkish, and Farsi in the airline, retail, telecom, and banking domains. We natively localize every layer of the benchmark: customer databases are populated with culturally appropriate records, user-simulator prompts are refined iteratively through contrastive annotation by native-language experts, and tasks are updated according to the localized database and to reflect realistic tasks in the target region. Evaluation across eight agent models shows the largest drops compared to English in the Korean and Farsi retail domains, by up to 61 points in pass^4. Code and data released at https://github.com/lilt/tau-bench-lilt.

articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07218v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Adolescents are increasingly turning to AI chatbots for mental health support, advice, and companionship, raising safety concerns. While recent evaluations have started to examine safety across multiple conversational turns, few compare how slight changes in a teen's responses can affect a chatbot's safety in the same scenario. We conduct a clinician-informed evaluation of chatbot safety in simulated conversations with adolescents aged 13-17, examining how safety failures vary with adolescents' responses and teen-aware system prompting. We evaluated 32,555 simulated conversations across 18 chatbot APIs and two system-prompt conditions using 22 safety criteria grounded in previously identified harms. Conversations spanned 983 variants of 106 seed scenarios covering urgent safety issues, health advice, and identity and relationships. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07228v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: User inference asks whether a source contributed documents to a language-model update, even when the auditor observes only fresh documents from that source. Document-level scores can provide evidence of participation, but combining this evidence is challenging: documents differ in baseline predictability and in how strongly they reflect information learned from other documents of the same source. We propose source-balanced capped Fisher (SCF), an aggregation method that uses known nonparticipating sources to assess how unusual each document score is. It transforms the resulting reference-tail frequencies into negative-log evidence, caps individual contributions, and averages them within each source. This limits the influence of isolated extreme scores while retaining evidence across multiple documents. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07232v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: At context lengths of about 1M tokens, dense attention is costly in prefill and decoding, and training typically relies on long documents, which become scarcer as the target length increases. Most sparse attention methods score all preceding blocks or tokens, so their selection cost per query is $O(L)$ at context length $L$; hierarchical selection reduces it to $O(\log L)$, but prior trainable hierarchical methods report accuracy only within their training length. We propose RecSA (Recursive Sparse Attention), which builds a tree over the KV cache in which each node summarizes its subtree with one key and one mean-pooled value. The keys come from one pooler per layer, shared by all levels and distilled from dense attention. Each level above the tokens selects at most $k$ candidates, so each query has $O(\log L)$ selection cost and reads $O(\log L)$ entries; the summaries of unselected candidates share one softmax with the exact tokens. articles.title: Archetypal contexts in the neurons of language models: an architecture for intelligence?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07234v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We validate our previous hypothesis that a language model holds relational patterns apart from the subject domains that instantiate them (Nordfors, 2026). These archetypal contexts are patterns of relations that people recognize across many fields, such as the tipping point or winner takes all, held once and applied across domains. We show this inside the model, Qwen3.8-27B. One set of neurons carries the archetype, say the tipping point; another carries the topic, say politics, ecology or cell biology; a third carries the language, such as English, Spanish or Chinese. Silence the tipping point's neurons, and the model no longer identifies the pattern but still knows what the text is about. Silence the topic's, and it loses the topic but still names the pattern. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07238v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI agents may consume massive tokens across a wide range of tasks, but how many of those tokens are really necessary? Although prior work has shown that agents can incur unexpectedly high token costs, we still lack a systematic way to identify and measure token waste. In this work, we introduce a unified framework for measuring token waste across heterogeneous agent systems. Our framework records and normalizes complete agent trajectories, identifies removable spans using an LLM-as-a-Judge (LLMaJ), and maps the identified text spans back to the original trajectory for token-level measurement. We validate the identified waste through direct interventions by removing marked spans, resuming agent execution, and measuring changes in task outcomes and subsequent actions. Abstract: Parallel block drafting accelerates speculative decoding by predicting multiple future positions in a single backbone pass, but on-device deployment constrains both drafter capacity and context storage. Under tight memory budgets, drafters must model long-range dependencies and fine-grained draft-position interactions without the growing KV-cache overhead of full-context attention. We propose HyFlash, a compact parallel drafter that introduces a prefix-memory prior to separate long-range context modeling from fine-grained draft-position interactions with limited capacity. Local attention captures recent context and draft-position interactions, while recurrent memory compresses historical target features into fixed-size states. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07453v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Test-time compute (TTC) improves language model responses by spending additional computation at inference time, and the right amount of compute depends on the prompt. Adaptive TTC methods allocate compute based on signals of response quality such as observed rewards, often by stopping once the signal exceeds a fixed threshold, and generally measure cost by the number of generations or tokens. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07461v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives. Abstract: Long-horizon role-playing dialogue requires consistent character identity, reliable memory, and context-sensitive interaction. We present a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) framework that revises original-character memory, stable persona instructions, and a policy for constructing turn-level prompts. Across the pooled evaluated replies, the bad-response rate decreases from 14.00% (6,973/49,824) to 4.94% (2,459/49,793), a 9.06-percentage-point reduction and a 64.71% relative reduction. articles.title: T$^2$-Splat: Adaptive Topology Mesh Splatting with Texture Residuals
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.06974v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Triangle-based splatting connects novel view synthesis with conventional graphics pipelines, but often requires excessive tessellation to preserve appearance details. We present T$^2$-Splat, which decouples topology adaptation from appearance refinement. Safe Restricted Delaunay Triangulation (Safe RDT) initializes mesh connectivity. Dynamic Topology Evolution (DTE) then adapts triangle allocation through edge collapse and vertex split operations. Residual per-face Mip-textures then refine appearance on the fixed mesh using scale-adaptive filtering. Experiments on Mip-NeRF 360, Tanks & Temples, and DTU demonstrate competitive results with compact meshes. T$^2$-Splat improves PSNR by 0.71dB over MeshSplatting on Mip-NeRF 360. Additional compression experiments demonstrate flexible control of mesh complexity, supporting face budgets as low as 10% of the original face count. Project page: https://t2-splat.github.io/.

Abstract: Transductive adaptation improves vision-language models at test time by refining predictions on an unlabeled batch, but current methods face a key trade-off. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07009v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Video understanding models often rely on motion, yet their explanations can obscure which motion sources support a prediction. We identify motion-source under-specification as a limitation of existing video XAI: region-centric explanations can be source-ambiguous, while motion vocabularies restricted to single-person pose sequences are source-incomplete. We propose TraCE (Trajectory-Aware Concepts for Explainable Video Understanding), a concept-based framework that discovers source-flexible motion concepts by clustering optical-flow trajectories from training videos. These concepts represent dynamic evidence from people, objects, and interactions, while object and scene concepts account for static context. The resulting typed trajectory/object/scene interface supports class prediction for action recognition and question-conditioned concept matching for video question answering (VQA). Abstract: Hybrid Mesh-Gaussian rendering combines compact textured surfaces with flexible 3D Gaussian primitives, offering an efficient alternative to purely Gaussian scene representations for structured environments. Existing scene-reconstruction hybrids commonly follow an additive formulation, where Gaussian residuals compensate for errors left by the mesh. However, not every Mesh-Gaussian conflict is caused by missing content: residual geometry errors, occlusion mismatch, texture-projection artifacts, and view-dependent appearance can make the same mesh content consistent in one view but inconsistent in another. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07055v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Flow matching (FM) generators often face a quality-coverage tradeoff. Inference-time techniques such as classifier-free guidance raise quality, but at the cost of coverage. We hypothesize this limitation stems from a basic property of the objective: an intermediate noisy image could correspond to many clean images, yet the model can only predict a single velocity, at best averaging over the multiple possibilities. To mitigate this, we introduce competition among predictions during training. We achieve this by augmenting the predictor with a randomly drawn low-dimensional conditioning code $z$. For each training example, we sample $K$ values of $z$ to produce $K$ candidate velocities that compete to explain the target, and apply the loss only to the best-matching candidate. Abstract: Skin lesion segmentation without annotated masks requires the target to be specified through other cues. Existing approaches rely on dermoscopy-specific rules, annotation-derived model priors, or user-selected regions. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07063v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level structure. Conversely, structure-aware methods exploit local evidence but often introduce additional inference-time computation. We propose SD-LoRA, a structural distillation framework that uses token-level graph reasoning only during training and transfers its effects into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model. arXiv:2611.07081v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multi-perspective-camera systems are widely adopted since they provide broad visual coverage for autonomous driving, motivating the synthesis of a unified wide view from spatially separated observations. In this work, we formulate wide view synthesis (WVS), which aims to synthesize a geometrically consistent wide view at a specified virtual viewpoint from multiple perspective cameras. Unlike conventional image stitching, WVS requires reasoning about 3D geometry and visibility to handle depth-dependent parallax and occlusions arising from spatially separated camera centers. While vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity view synthesis, its reliance on per-scene optimization limits its applicability to driving scenes. Abstract: We present an automated method for auditing text-to-image generators for representational bias against ground-truth demographic benchmarks. Our approach adapts the racial proxy variables used in U.S. antidiscrimination law to provide a fine-grained comparative analysis of variations in racial representation in generated images. We classify each generated image by race and then compare the model's distribution to publicly available demographic benchmark data to identify patterns of over- and under-representation. We also measure skin tone using CIELAB values and calculate cosine similarity amongst groups of images in order to capture biases that don't show up in demographic comparisons such as differences in image quality across races and skin tones. Abstract: Recent works in neural video coding have increasingly been trading off perceptual quality against reconstruction fidelity at a fixed bitrate. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07176v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Self-supervised learning has given rise to vision foundation models that learn general-purpose image representations transferable across downstream tasks, yet representation learning for 3D scenes has not achieved comparable success. Motivated by this, we identify key limitations of current 3D representation learning approaches and revisit their core design choices. We first replace the commonly used hierarchical PTv3 backbone with the Volume Transformer, a ViT-like architecture for 3D scenes. We then redesign two core objectives of modern approaches built around student-teacher networks: matching representations across views and predicting masked content from visible context. For the first objective, we separate the roles of teacher and student: the teacher provides clean, consistent targets while the student learns invariance to stronger perturbations. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07188v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Radiologists read a screening mammogram by first forming a global impression of the four views and then selectively magnifying suspicious regions before assigning a BI-RADS assessment. MLLMs, in contrast, see the whole image at a fixed, reduced resolution, which makes sub-millimeter calcifications invisible, and they perform close to chance on mammography. Therefore, we present MammoSeek, a mammography agent that reproduces this reading process. After forming an impression of each breast, the agent performs selective zooming: it decides by itself which detector candidates deserve a closer look and inspects only those on full-resolution views. Guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, it then assigns a category and generates a localized, lexicon-structured report for each breast; its assessment is combined with image-model scores in a decision layer to decide recall. Abstract: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07301v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning has become an effective approach for improving video generation, but its success depends heavily on reliable reward models. Existing methods either map videos directly to opaque scalar scores or generate free-form rationales that are not explicitly optimized as the basis of the final judgment. We propose ArtiVidRM, a verifiable, artifact-as-rubrics video reward model that follows an observe-then-score paradigm. It first identifies visible generation artifacts and organizes them into a structured artifact list, then uses these artifacts as explicit rubrics for quality assessment. Abstract: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. Abstract: Solving visual puzzles requires both accurate interpretation of visual evidence and reliable computation under task-specific rules. Embedding visual assumptions and task constraints directly in solving code makes the represented problem difficult to inspect and revise independently. We introduce Vis2State, a training-free agentic framework that abstracts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states linking visual inspection and execution. Visual inspection guides state construction and refinement, while generated programs solve the represented problem. The model constructs both the state and the program without predefined puzzle schemas or solving procedures. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.07398v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. Existing methods either invert explicit scattering variables, which can be unstable under complex scenes, or learn direct restoration mappings, which often discard the physical organization of haze formation. We present \emph{FreePath}, a neural mean free path framework for image dehazing. Instead of estimating atmospheric parameters, FreePath represents dehazing as feature space path state restoration, inspired by the expected distance a visual response can propagate before interacting with haze. Within a residual encoder and decoder, the Mean Free Path Residual Block learns path and collision fields to guide haze constrained correction, while FreePath State Conservation Integration preserves restored path states during deep feature aggregation. Abstract: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. Abstract: Robot imitation learning is limited by the scarcity of action-labeled data, while action-free demonstrations such as videos are abundant. Recent latent-action methods learn action-relevant representations from observation transitions, but they do not optimize latent actions for downstream control, leading to latent representations that are difficult for policies to model and difficult to accurately decode into continuous robot actions. Abstract: This paper presents Proactive Human-in-the-Loop (PHIL), a framework for proactive policy correction and preference-based post-training. PHIL enables operators to preview policy-predicted future motion and intervene before anticipated undesirable actions. PHIL pairs rejected policy predictions with corrective action chunks subsequently executed from the same physical state over the same horizon, and preference-based post-training encourages the policy to favor these corrections. Abstract: Olfaction provides critical information about airborne chemical cues, yet it remains largely underexplored in embodied AI, with limited prior machine olfaction work focusing primarily on semantic odor perception. Abstract: Motor responses evoked by noxious stimulation are used to assess neurological function in hospitalized patients with disorders of consciousness. Abstract: We study physics-based retargeting of human demonstrations for robot learning: finding robot controls that reproduce reference motions under contact dynamics. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05793v2 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Short-horizon model predictive control (MPC) is fast but myopic. ZipMPC compensates by learning a context-dependent correction of the short-horizon cost that imitates a long-horizon expert. We observe that the optimal correction is often multimodal: when a slower opponent can be passed on either side, good corrections of opposite sign coexist, and the expert's choice between them hinges on tiny cost differences. Deterministic regression then averages modes or inherits inconsistent expert tie-breaking. We propose ZipDrift, which trains a one-step drifting generator over MPC cost corrections, tilted toward low closed-loop cost and learned only from cost evaluations of candidate corrections, without differentiating through the optimiser. articles.content:

Abstract: Assessing the deployment performance of learned robot policies during training is challenging, as directly measuring task success requires costly real-world trials for each candidate checkpoint. Abstract: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) support planning by comparing predicted latent states with an encoded goal. articles.title: Does RRT* Work on Uneven Terrain Meshes?
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05885v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The optimal rapidly exploring random tree (RRT*) is proven asymptotically optimal on open subsets of Euclidean space with straight-line local planning. We ask whether it works on a triangle-mesh terrain, a two-dimensional surface in R^3. First, the original RRT* cannot run on a mesh: the surface has zero volume, so uniform sampling never hits it, no clearance ball fits in it, and chords across a fold leave it. Abstract: An ordered sequence of end-effector poses can give a redundant robot arm multiple valid joint configurations at each waypoint. Inverse kinematics (IK) computes these configurations. Choosing a configuration only for the next waypoint can leave the arm poorly placed for later waypoints. This may increase planned motion time or cause a later planning failure. This paper presents Future-Window Inverse Kinematics (FWIK), an online method that selects IK solutions by considering a small window of future waypoints. FWIK generates several IK candidates, connects them in a layered joint-space graph, and ranks candidate paths with a simple motion-time estimate. A learned model removes paths whose transitions are likely to cause self-collision. Abstract: Off-policy deep reinforcement learning trains on random samples from a replay buffer of past experience. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05936v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Integrating six-axis tactile feedback into robotic interfaces requires compact sensors with accurate load measurement and rapid online reconstruction. This paper presents LumiTac, a low-profile, camera-free optoelectronic tactile sensor combining spatially distributed illumination with spectral encoding. Five photoemitters and five RGBW photoreceivers are mounted on opposing circuit boards coupled through translucent silicone. Load-induced interlayer motion modulates the internal light field under compression, shear, bending, and torsion. The sensing head measures 12 mm in diameter and 4.75 mm in thickness, weighs less than 2 g, and has a component cost of approximately USD 7. A compact multilayer perceptron reconstructs three force and three moment components from 20 optical channels. articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05938v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Visual-inertial odometry relies on visual features that correspond to 3D points with consistent projections across sequential frames. In reflective indoor-floor environments, however, specular floor patterns can be detected and triangulated as virtual features below the physical ground plane, producing unreliable feature associations and inconsistent visual residuals. articles.title: Learning Object-Centric Motion Priors from Human for Robotic Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.05979v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Manipulating diverse objects with multi-fingered dexterous hands is challenging due to the high dimensionality and complex dynamics. Human-Object Interaction (HOI) datasets provide rich knowledge about task information and embodied interactions. Instead of solely imitating the human demonstrations, our method learns to holistically predict future hand-object states by leveraging these datasets. The predicted future states of the object can serve as a general-purpose reward term for reinforcement learning, reducing reliance on task-specific reward engineering and enhancing generalization across tasks. We conduct extensive experiments on three manipulation tasks in simulation and the real world. Our approach outperforms existing SOTA methods in both success rate and generalizability on novel objects. Furthermore, we validate the cross-embodiment compatibility of our methods by successfully deploying the skills on different robot hands.

articles.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
articles.content: User embeddings are central components of modern recommendation, personalization, and behavioral modeling systems. Though these embeddings can compactly encode rich behavioral information, they are inherently dense and opaque, limiting interpretability. To address this gap, we argue that user embeddings can be understood as sparse superpositions of interpretable behavioral modes. This structure is directly predicted by generative models of user behavior for linear embeddings and extends approximately to deep-learning representations by the superposition hypothesis. Superimposed modes can naturally be recovered by sparse dictionary learning methods, such as sparse autoencoders (SAEs), and recovered modes can be automatically named and queried in natural language. We validate mode recovery against known ground truth on synthetic data, where SAEs recover modes better than classical sparse baselines, including on transformer-encoded embeddings. We then apply the method to classical and transformer-based user embeddings from two real-world datasets. We also show how the corresponding natural-language labels enable zero-shot audience retrieval and characterization over embeddings never trained on text. The framework is post-hoc and model-agnostic, requiring no modification to the upstream embedding system.

articles.title: Do You Miss the Nights We Spent Crafting Figures? Rethinking Teaser and Framework Figures in the Age of Generative AI
articles.content: Scientific figures give research ideas a visual form through choices of abstraction, composition, and emphasis. Generative AI offers new ways to realize these choices, raising questions about explanatory clarity and purposeful visual expression. We examine these questions through a visual retrospective of 371 motivation and framework figures from 200 papers. The corpus comprises a quota-based main sample of 160 papers spanning four temporal periods and a separate purposive style-contrast sample of 40 papers. A single multimodal judge evaluates six dimensions of communication and design, with three repeated judgments per figure. We attempt source-constrained revisions of all 371 figures, of which 369 pass the recorded fidelity checks. Original-figure ratings show no uniform decline across periods. Revisions increase mean clarity ratings by 0.428 points and decrease aesthetic coherence ratings by 0.111 points on a five-point scale. Gains in the six-dimension average are larger for main-sample motivation figures than for frameworks. Case analyses show that added explanation can clarify comparisons while leaving typographic hierarchy and visual economy unresolved. These model-based findings support researcher-led design, with AI assisting exploration and authors retaining responsibility for explanatory purpose, composition, and scientific relationships. The accompanying atlas and evaluation records are available at https://ntu-ai4x.github.io/Rethinking_Figures/index_en.html.

articles.title: Where and Why is Grounded Reasoning Useful?
articles.content: Grounded reasoning, where a model outputs text coordinates of relevant locations in chain-of-thought reasoning, is a common strategy for solving complex visual reasoning problems. However, the benefits and limitations of grounded reasoning are understudied. We study where and why grounded reasoning is most useful. To do so, we introduce a chain-of-thought analysis method to measure how much a model uses its outputted grounding in its thinking trace and perform a detailed ablation study of a grounded reasoning training recipe. We find that grounded reasoning improves counting but shows no significant gain over baselines without coordinate grounding across a wide range of spatial reasoning and perception benchmarks. Using several synthetic tasks, we show that grounded reasoning is most useful when a task requires undescribable references, which are visual concepts that are difficult to describe in language. However, we observe that many existing visual reasoning benchmarks are solvable with only describable text references. To close this gap, we introduce BrickVision, a new benchmark that requires undescribable visual references to solve.

articles.title: SwarmEvolve: Latent Agent Swarms for Evolutionary Discovery and Optimization
articles.content: LLM-guided evolutionary search uses AI agents to improve programs for mathematical and computational problems by iteratively refining solutions and combining high-scoring methods. However, the process is often slow because the LLM generates a long textual chain of thought for each round and must repeat this generation many times to maintain population diversity. We present SwarmEvolve, a framework in which hundreds of low-cost agents per round work in swarms, reason in latent space without decoding to text, and share information by passing KV caches. Each swarm studies the problem from a different angle. A novelty filter keeps the most distinct agent ideas by directly measuring the distances between the agents' hidden state vectors. Crossover of ideas happens naturally in latent space, as a summarizer agent receives the combined KV caches of all swarm members. On 21 problems in mathematical discovery and scientific computing, SwarmEvolve gets the highest average score and needs a median of only 3 to 8 minutes to reach the best scores that other state-of-the-art frameworks reach in 60 minutes. On several problems, SwarmEvolve with Qwen3 8B improves on the solutions that AlphaEvolve first found with frontier LLMs. Our work shows that agent swarms that communicate in latent space offer a fast, low-cost approach to program search for scientific problems.

articles.title: Scientist World: Grow a Research World for AI-Scientists
articles.content: AI-Scientists arrived, but a world for them to grow in did not. Human scientists take theirs for granted $-$ centuries of open problems and shared ideas, waiting in the scientific literature. To AI-Scientists, that world is readable but not runnable, so we build Scientist World for them: every research paper becomes an executable environment. Our autonomous pipeline extracts each paper's open-ended research question and reproduces its proposed method as the baseline; an AI-Scientist entering the environment is evaluated against what the human authors achieved. We release the first 1,000 verified environments. With the world as an evaluation, we found that frontier AI-Scientists can already surpass the human researchers 74% of the time. As a record of how AI does science, it contains 6,400 hours of research traces, with every idea, experiment, failure, and success. As a training ground, we are able to raise (+158%) a small model to match frontier models in research ideation. At last, AI-Scientists' own world has arrived, grown from and growing with science itself.

articles.title: EgoGeneralist: Unifying Egocentric Action-Video Tasks through Video-Native Modeling
articles.content: Modern video models possess strong visual priors, yet do not natively represent human action in metric 3D space. We present EgoGeneralist, which adapts pretrained video generators to unify action-conditioned egocentric video generation, pose estimation, and joint action-video generation. Our role-adaptive action renderer provides video-native representations for multidirectional action-video learning, making metric motion usable as both a spatial control signal and a recoverable generation target. Cross-stream action-video coupling establishes close correspondence between metric motion and visual dynamics through lightweight adaptation while preserving the pretrained visual prior. Together, these designs establish a generalist framework spanning five action-video tasks. Despite adaptation only on controlled laboratory recordings, EgoGeneralist generalizes to diverse unseen scenes and interactions with effective action control and visual quality, bridging pretrained visual knowledge and metric 3D human motion.

articles.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
articles.content: ML code should run where researchers choose, not where it was first written. Today, machine learning code mainly lives in two ecosystems, PyTorch on NVIDIA GPUs and JAX on Google TPUs. Migrating repositories between them means building and testing across frameworks and hardware. This migration is (1) a practical need, since it unlocks different hardware for researchers, and (2) a natural benchmark: it involves different frameworks and hardware, covers whole repositories, and is long-horizon and challenging. We introduce XStack, a benchmark that evaluates agents on migrating ML repositories between these two ecosystems. Each agent receives a PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine and must deliver a JAX repository. Its output passes if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository's published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.

articles.title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
articles.content: Interpretability, AI auditing and assessments of machine consciousness increasingly rest on mechanism-level quantities: functionals of a system's causal transition law that describe how it computes, not what it outputs. Experiments see that law only through finite, partial and noisy interventions. We ask when such a quantity is identifiable from an experiment's access, continuous in the mechanism and certifiable from finite data, and answer exactly for a deliberately demanding case - the integrated information $\varphi$ of integrated information theory - in stochastic networks of four and five units with known ground truth. Behavior can be silent: a recurrent and a feed-forward network with identical input-output laws at their response delay carry 0.28 and 0 bits, yet internal recordings separate them within 4-53 trials. Partial access can be just as blind: in our examples, units left out of a one-step recording impose precision floors of 0.30-1.02 bits that no sample size lowers, and in all-but-self parity networks, recordings of any length see several hidden units only through the product of their fidelities - a symmetry that one intervention broke in exact checks. The measure has sharp edges: because $\varphi$ selects a partition, and the cause and effect it specifies, by one criterion and reports another, infinitesimal changes of mechanism that cross an edge change it by 25-100% at 99% of the edges we found in random networks, and about 1% of surrogate models that fit interventional data almost perfectly misreport it by more than 20%. One-sided claims survive: the same data certify a lower bound on both sides of an edge, and we prove $\varphi>1.004$ bits throughout a 64-dimensional region of mechanisms and certify it from about $10^7$ controlled transitions with false-certificate probability at most $α$. Measurability is thus a design question with computable answers.

articles.title: Towards interpreting any residual stream direction by scaling activation inversion
articles.content: To interpret a direction in a language model's residual stream, we can look for text that strongly activates it. But when such text is found by scanning a corpus, it is limited to what that corpus contains. We develop Maximally-Activating Example Metamodels (MAEMs), language models which map residual stream directions from a subject model to text exemplars that strongly activate those directions. Our objective is to maximise the cosine similarity of a supplied residual stream direction with the activations of the text generated by the MAEM. This label-free RL objective helps to scale MAEMs on diverse sources of residual stream directions. Empirically, we find the resultant metamodel produces informative exemplars: a Qwen3.6-27B MAEM inverts held-out activations better than corpus search or a natural-language autoencoder (NLA), beats corpus search (at 10M tokens) on a majority of held-out languages/domains, and activates 89% of held-out SAE features. It also identifies concepts behind steering vectors about as well as NLAs, recovers the payloads of LoRA backdoors more often than corpus search, and can even verbalise some model workspace inner monologue. Unlike explanations produced by other metamodels (e.g. NLAs), MAEM exemplars can be verified with a forward pass on the subject model, making the MAEM objective a grounded alternative for scaling the training of metamodels.

articles.title: OopsieRecover: Learning Transferable VLA Corrections from Semantic Interventions
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models can perform a wide range of robotic manipulation tasks, but often fail during deployment. Teaching them to recover from these failures requires substantial corrective data: existing approaches learn to recover from failures by directly associating corrective actions with the observations in which they were demonstrated. For instance, DAgger-like fine-tuning can require tens to hundreds of interactions, yet the resulting policy may still fail to generalize the learned corrections beyond the demonstrated scenarios. We hypothesize that semantics can capture the underlying reasons for failures and their corrections, enabling policies to learn from only a handful of corrective demonstrations and generalize those corrections to novel objects, and scene variations. We propose OopsieRecover, a framework that uses abduction to infer the intent behind a small set of corrective demonstrations and encodes the inferred knowledge as dense spatial representations and conditional costs. These costs capture when a behavior is undesirable and steer the policy toward more desirable action regions. We experiment across 6 tasks and variations in object poses, scenes, and related tasks, and find that only a handful of corrective demonstrations can enable a VLA to overcome failures across a broad range of novel situations, without requiring new corrective data for each variation. Please refer to https://robin-lab.cs.utexas.edu/oopsierecover for videos.
