articles.title: Latent RL Priors for Data-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation
articles.content: Learning dexterous manipulation from limited visual demonstrations is challenging because policies must acquire both perceptual grounding and precise control, while reinforcement learning (RL) in simulation can acquire rich control behaviors from large-scale interaction with privileged information. We introduce \textbf{Latent RL Prior}, a two-stage framework that reuses this control knowledge for data-efficient visual policy learning. During privileged pretraining, we distill large-scale RL rollouts into a flow-matching action decoder conditioned on proprioception and latent task context. During visual adaptation, we freeze the decoder and learn a visual interface that maps images to its latent context using action supervision alone, without privileged labels or latent targets. The same decoder can further be shared across arms by learning coordinated visual contexts for bimanual manipulation. Across three simulated tasks, our method outperforms full-parameter fine-tuning of $π_{0.5}$ and GR00T N1.7 in the low-data regime; on door lifting and bimanual assembly, it surpasses full-data baselines using $10\times$ and $5\times$ fewer demonstrations, respectively. Further analysis shows that direct visual-to-latent conditioning improves adaptation performance and training stability over routing visual predictions through the pretrained state encoder. Robustness to unseen mass variation and greater linear accessibility of contact-force information in decoder representations further provide evidence of retained RL-acquired control knowledge. Project website: https://yixiaowang7.github.io/latent-rl-prior-page/.

articles.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
articles.content: Adversarial Training (AT) is an important method for improving model robustness. We study the dynamics of deterministic Gradient Descent (GD) in AT. Most existing works in this direction focus on the small or vanishing step sizes regime, where GD resembles a continuous-time flow. However, such step sizes can make training inefficient and are rarely used in practice. In this paper, we study the AT dynamics of GD with large constant step sizes. We first study GD in adversarial linear logistic regression, focusing on two aspects: where the model parameters converge (implicit bias) and how quickly the losses decrease (optimization). We then turn to neural networks training and study how the sharpness of losses evolve during AT. Our results advance the understanding of the behaviors of GD with large step sizes in AT and highlight three key differences from its behavior in Standard Training (ST): (i) the implicit bias gap between AT and ST, previously established only for small step sizes, persists for arbitrarily large constant step sizes, (ii) different from ST, there is no uniform rate of convergence for the optimization error in AT, and (iii) sharpness can exhibit two-stage dynamics that differ from the Edge-of-Stability behavior observed in ST.

articles.title: Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO
articles.content: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision. Does this dense signal reduce the training FLOPs needed to reach a target accuracy compared with reinforcement learning? We systematically compare vanilla reverse-KL OPD with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs. With an external post-trained teacher, OPD generally loses to GRPO in accuracy per training FLOP at matched settings, even when the teacher is further trained with GRPO, and often suffers response-length inflation. Yet a different teacher changes the picture: when the teacher is the student's own GRPO checkpoint, OPD recovers that checkpoint's accuracy on math with $50\times$ fewer distillation FLOPs than GRPO needs to reach the same accuracy. Following the same teacher setting, we consistently observe this high efficiency with a larger student, on code, and in a second model family. On a single domain, however, the GRPO checkpoint is already the desired model, so distilling it adds to total compute. Across domains, separate GRPO checkpoints hold different capabilities, and no single checkpoint serves every domain. Multi-teacher OPD (DeepSeek-AI, 2026) consolidates per-domain GRPO experts into a single student that matches each expert's accuracy, with the distillation stage costing only 5.2% (on 2 domains) and 8.0% (on 4 domains) of the specialist training FLOPs. Counting specialist training and distillation together, this pipeline reaches joint GRPO's performance on the 2-domain mix with 42.0% fewer total FLOPs.

articles.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
articles.content: Reproducing machine learning experiments requires reconstructing procedures from information scattered across papers, released code, and supporting artifacts. For coding agents, reproduction success can therefore depend on their ability to fill in missing details, rather than on the released artifacts alone. We ask whether preserving recovered procedures and decisions improves subsequent independent reproduction. We define a standardized artifact design comprising a refined codebase, environment setup, experiment launchers, and a reproduction guide, and introduce ReproBridge, an agent workflow for constructing these refined reproducible artifacts. ReproBridge-Bench provides 1,029 tasks from 387 experiments across 36 papers, anchored by five human-verified reference scores per task. Agents attempt tasks in fresh sessions with raw code or refined artifacts; a separate Auditor checks execution evidence. Across four evaluated models, refined artifacts raise mean reproduction success from 76.4% to 92.6% and reduce downstream API spending by 19.7% on average. The cross-model success-rate spread narrows from 21.6 to 3.9 percentage points, with all four models achieving mean success rates above 90%. Removing any component reduces success in the ablation study, with the largest losses from code and environment removal. These results suggest that preserving execution knowledge helps even models with lower raw-code success reproduce experiments more reliably and at lower API cost.

articles.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
articles.content: Models for physical AI tasks, such as robotics and autonomous driving, need not reason solely in language. They can use visual plans--points, bounding boxes, and trajectories--to represent spatial goals and anticipate motion. However, autoregressive vision-language models generate these plans one coordinate token at a time, making richer predictions increasingly costly. We introduce VFlash, a method for fast, accurate visual planning through Flash Primitive Decoding. VFlash exploits the known structure of visual primitives to predict their coordinates jointly, using a lightweight drafter that generates an entire primitive in one forward pass. The layout adapts to the primitive's type, dimensionality, and length, supporting compact boxes and long, variable-length trajectories. Crucially, spatial accuracy need not require reproducing an autoregressive model's exact token sequence. VFlash therefore trains on annotated primitives and directly accepts structurally valid predictions without target-token agreement. Across the evaluated 2D and 3D robot trajectory tasks, VFlash consistently reduces prediction errors relative to autoregressive decoding. Preliminary single-rollout measurements indicate approximately 25x faster generation for 3D point motion forecasting. A world action model conditioned on VFlash plans achieves 70.2% average success across four MolmoSpaces task suites, compared with 62.6% for the baseline.

articles.title: A Hidden Markov Preference Model for Online Prediction of Adversary Actions
articles.content: A defender anticipating an attacker needs a probability distribution over the attacker's next action from information available before that action occurs. Two structures complicate this: the attacker's behavioral regime persists and can switch within an episode, and each action combines an operation with state-dependent arguments whose feasible values change over time. We capture both with a hidden Markov model whose latent state is the active regime and whose regime-conditioned action law is defined on a feasibility-masked tree of executable actions. The same likelihood forms the next-action distribution and updates the regime belief once the action is seen, and a partially observed prefix contributes its resolved local factors. Estimation separates into convex logistic fits that Baum-Welch reuses when regimes are unlabeled. We derive a reach-weighted nodewise KL expression for regime information, a sequence-wise log-loss bound for switching regime paths, and a uniform fallback guarantee. On the CAGE 2 cyber defense benchmark the filtered latent state is worth 0.8 nats per step, and after a controller switch the loss begins to fall in three steps against ten for a recurrent baseline.

articles.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
articles.content: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. We present an edge-assisted crowdsensing system: handlebar cameras supply street-level frames, a vision-language model (VLM) turns each frame into structured traffic attributes through a single prompt, and an explainable boosting machine (EBM) combines them with OpenStreetMap road infrastructure and on-bike kinematics to predict a crowdsourced 1-9 safety score. Extraction belongs at the network edge: the fastest self-hosted model needs 2.49 s per frame and scoring takes 0.4 ms on a CPU. On 1,362 annotated frames from two London routes, the EBM regressor reaches 72.2 percent binary accuracy and a mean absolute error of 1.011 under five-fold cross-validation. It is within one accuracy point of black-box ensembles. Its per-feature shape functions give exact attribution: physical lane separation is worth +0.97 rating points, a painted lane +0.70 and a construction site -0.65. Planners can therefore price an infrastructure change in rating points, and the results enter cost-benefit analysis directly. We also report inter-annotator agreement (alpha = 0.4695), an attribute audit, and a sensitivity analysis linking attribute error to accuracy. With re-encoding, a 20 s sampling interval serves 1,000 riders at 54 Mbit/s at a cost of 1.4 accuracy points, making continuous monitoring practical.

articles.title: Label-Wording Augmentation in a Typed-Decision Encoder: Gains on Unfamiliar Words, Not on Abbreviations or Codes
articles.content: Typed-decision models score options that the caller supplies at request time, so their accuracy depends on label wording that the model's developer does not control. We compare two releases of a 307M-parameter multilingual cross-encoder, Ru-Jev, trained on thirteen Russian-language tasks; the later release adds an augmentation that presents labels in several surface forms. Holding questions fixed and varying only how eighteen routing labels are worded, we evaluate ten label vocabularies, produced by three separate processes and checked for overlap with the training data, with five candidates per question and, for eight of them, also with eighteen. On held-out vocabularies made of ordinary or borrowed words (English-derived jargon, office slang, department names), the augmented release is more accurate in every setting, by up to 0.24. Eleven of these fourteen gains survive a Holm correction (slang with eighteen candidates and descriptive sentences with five do not), and for jargon on all labels the label-level interval excludes zero in both settings. On abbreviations and opaque codes it gives no usable gain: on abbreviations it is not better, and worse on the clean slice, and on opaque codes both releases stay at or below chance once labels related to training options are removed. In most cells where accuracy rises, the risk-coverage area falls, but with eighteen candidates confident errors rise on jargon and slang. On two datasets neither release saw, accuracy moves by -8.4 and +5.6 points. We also report four evaluation hazards from comparing the two releases.

articles.title: Understanding AI from the Inside: The State of Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety
articles.content: Neural networks are likely to be among the most consequential artefacts in human history. As these systems become more capable and autonomous, their potential to cause societal harm also grows, making AI safety one of the defining challenges of our time. Yet we continue to build increasingly powerful systems without fully understanding how they work, how they will behave in unfamiliar situations, or how to reliably control them. Mechanistic interpretability offers a path towards understanding these systems by studying their internal representations and computations, with the aim of evaluating, predicting, and controlling behaviour. We survey mechanistic interpretability for AI safety in order to answer the question: Does understanding how models work actually make them safer? We place mechanistic interpretability in the broader context of interpretability research and compare its mechanistic evidence with behavioural evaluation. We introduce the foundations of mechanistic interpretability, including features, polysemanticity, transformer computation, and circuits, and survey methods for feature extraction and analysis, circuit discovery and causal verification, explaining intermediate representations in natural language, learning dynamics, and training-data attribution. Beyond surveying existing methods, we propose a unified framework for evaluating mechanistic interpretability claims and characterise six research orientations by their goals, assumptions, and trade-offs. Finally, we examine how mechanistic understanding can support AI safety, including knowledge editing, steering, and monitoring, and assess its limitations, failure modes, open problems, and relationship to behavioural safety measures. We also release a repository of code notebooks with worked examples that reproduce key findings from surveyed methods, allowing readers to build intuition through hands-on experimentation.

articles.title: SM4RT: Cascaded Feed-forward Model for 4D Reconstruction
articles.content: We introduce SM4RT, a multi-task cascade feed-forward model for dynamic scene reconstruction from RGB videos. While existing feed-forward approaches typically address geometry reconstruction and motion estimation separately--and often predict motions in a single coordinate frame that must account for camera movement--SM4RT solves these tasks sequentially by first reconstructing 3D geometry and then bootstrapping motion estimation from the predicted structure. By expressing each pixel's 3D motion in its corresponding camera frame, SM4RT reduces ambiguity arising from camera motion. To address the sparsity of real-world motion labels, SM4RT further incorporates a weakly supervised loss that regularizes unlabeled point motions using labeled point positions at the other time step. We evaluate motion estimation on three dynamic-scene datasets--Kubric, Waymo, and Point Odyssey--and SM4RT achieves the best performance on most metrics compared with prior baselines. We additionally benchmark geometry reconstruction on five dynamic scene datasets and show that SM4RT achieves competitive performance with state-of-the-art methods. Overall, our unified framework demonstrates that combining geometry reconstruction and motion estimation in a cascade not only avoids performance trade-offs but also enhances motion estimation through improved geometric reasoning.

articles.title: MedGraph: Maintaining Patient State with Graph Memory for Long-Term Medical Dialogue
articles.content: LLM-based medical assistants that follow a patient across visits need a memory that keeps the patient's clinical state correct as it changes. We examine the errors of five memory systems on longitudinal medical dialogue and find three recurring causes: the retrieved evidence gives an outdated state, includes another person's health facts, or lacks a safety fact the answer depends on. We present MedGraph, a graph memory built for these three cases. Construction extracts dated facts from each session, attributes each fact to the person it describes, and links medication, diagnosis, and measurement records into chains that keep earlier states. Retrieval ranks the patient's chains as units, reads each chain at the time the question asks about, and adds the original dialogue text; a patient profile lists every recorded safety fact with every question. On MedMemoryBench, MedGraph has the highest overall accuracy with both a GPT and a Qwen backbone, 10.5 and 10.4 points above the strongest of five baselines, with efficient memory construction and answering in the GPT setting.

articles.title: The Power of Meta Access in the Software of the Future --- Demonstrated on LLM Chat UIs and Chat AI
articles.content: Chat remains the default surface for many large language model (LLM) tasks, even as agentic tools such as OpenCode excel at coding and automation. Yet the model sees the current dialogue but not the workspace around it. We explore meta access---giving the assistant a structured, permissioned view of the interface itself and propose a ladder of levels: feature tutoring; metadata, settings, and preference access; retrieval over summaries and messages, confirmed mutation, and full orchestration. Meta access can turn a chat client from many screens into one entry point for finding, navigating, organising, and operating it, while raising risks around grounding, privacy, prompt injection, and trust. General-purpose agentic harnesses are runtimes; because they can change their own settings, meta access becomes reflexive and needs a separate control-plane boundary. We ground this in the Meta Chat prototype of the Chat AI client. It builds bounded context from, e.g., summaries, settings, and relevant messages; links references to conversations, topics, and personas; supports confirmed, reversible changes; offers a browsable tutorial library; and recommends personas as user-started conversations. By exposing application state in structured form, meta access can extend screen readers from widget descriptions to semantic workspace operations. Meta access thus turns chat from a window onto one conversation into a control layer for the whole workspace, extending chat toward agentic capability without surrendering user control. As assistants become embedded in IDEs, dashboards, office suites, and operating systems, AI-era interfaces should expose a structured, permissioned model of their state and capabilities, ideally by opening their existing metamodels through a debugger-like interface.

articles.title: Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action models (VLAs) enable general-purpose embodied intelligence, but their performance is brittle under distribution shift, where unanticipated failures can damage equipment or endanger people. Deploying VLAs in real-world systems therefore requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, and informative while being efficient enough to run on the edge. Existing methods fail to fulfill these requirements. We present VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA backbone that improves early failure detection and bounds the missed-detection and false-alarm rates, with minimal inference overhead. We show that supervising on the pre-failure segment of a trajectory increases early failure detection at matched false-positive rates by up to 30% over the strongest learned baseline. Under shift to unseen tasks, the bounds on missed-detection and false-alarm rates remain valid in up to 86% of runs, versus at most 21% for baselines. Unlike existing methods, VLA-Tug predicts the failure mode to enable corrective actions, raising top-3 accuracy on unseen tasks by up to 44% over a majority baseline. VLA-Tug enables real-time monitoring where the well-timed and informative probe supports lightweight steering that improves task success. We release a dataset of 3,180 annotated manipulation episodes to support future work on latent failure detection in VLAs at https://vla-tug.github.io.

articles.title: Data-driven discovery of intrinsic Lie point symmetries of differential equation systems
articles.content: Discovering continuous symmetries directly from differential-equation data can reveal geometric structure for model reduction and scientific machine learning without symbolic determining equations or a closed-form representation of the governing system. We formulate intrinsic Lie point-symmetry discovery as an operator-theoretic problem on sampled jet-space data. Admissible generators are identified from a sampled determining operator and separated from redundant, solution-dependent, and geometrically trivial directions. The framework combines prolongation, sequential subspace restrictions, and a fixed nonlinear dictionary linear in trainable coefficients. A rank-stabilization preflight test diagnoses systems whose represented intrinsic symmetry algebra does not stabilize under dictionary refinement. On a controlled differential-equation benchmark with an analytically known 11-dimensional represented intrinsic symmetry algebra, the method recovers the complete represented generator set, reproduces its Lie-bracket structure to numerical precision, and approximates a known generator beyond the training domain. Here we show that explicit intrinsic continuous-symmetry generators can be recovered from data obtained from exact or approximate differential systems.

articles.title: On the limitations of molecular representations
articles.content: Molecular representations such as fingerprints and learned embeddings play a central role in cheminformatics and small-molecule machine learning. They serve as the primary input for a diverse array of tasks, including clustering, dataset splitting, and virtual screening, yet their evaluation is often limited to downstream model performance on narrow benchmark tasks. We carried out a systematic investigation of the quality of molecular representations, finding that none of the state-of-the-art molecular embedding models capture graph structure, 3D shape, or ADMET endpoint similarity better than fingerprints or physicochemical descriptors. However, classical fingerprints also revealed their own material limitations. For example, we show that depending on the representation, between 225M and $\sim$4B molecules have non-unique representations in the 10.8B Enamine REAL database, with implications for virtual screening. Our findings provide an insight into the current limitations of molecular representations, outlining future research directions for the development of more robust encodings of small molecules.

articles.title: Benchmarks as Software: Terminal-Bench and the Case for Continuous Benchmarks
articles.content: Coding agents are among the most economically consequential deployments of LLMs to date, making reliable evaluation increasingly important. Yet even benchmarks that are carefully validated at release can become stale. As models improve, they can discover valid solutions that existing verifiers reject, while changes to evaluation infrastructure can invalidate assumptions embedded in tasks and tests. We call the resulting accumulation of defects benchmark maintenance debt: a growing gap between benchmark scores and the capabilities they are intended to measure. We introduce a continuous-validation workflow for agentic benchmarks that combines community reports, task artifacts, agent traces, automated oracle checks, and human-gated repairs. We apply this workflow to Terminal-Bench 2.0, a benchmark that underwent extensive human and LM-assisted review and red-teaming before release. Our audit identifies issues in roughly 30% of the benchmark, and we release the resulting repairs as Terminal-Bench 2.1. These repairs change evaluation results: accuracy increased by over 10 percentage points and leaderboard positions move by up to three ranks, even as the overall ranking remains highly correlated (Spearman rho = 0.958).   We evaluate how resource allocation shapes benchmark conclusions. We show that fixed wall-clock can materially change agent performance: For example, extending the time limit closes a 20pp harness gap on GPT 5.4 and shrinks a 30 pp gap on GPT 5.4 mini to 5 pp. Benchmark maintenance is therefore not only about repairing task artifacts: resource budgets are part of the measurement specification and must be validated alongside the tasks themselves.   More broadly, benchmark maintenance debt is not just accumulated implementation bugs: our results show that as models improve, both evaluation assumptions and resource settings may need to be revalidated.

articles.title: Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is commonly used in both supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL), often under similar optimizer settings. Yet, how the different dynamics of the two stages manifest in the low-rank increment that LoRA optimizes remains unclear. Tracking the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates on mathematical reasoning tasks, we find that RL concentrates the spectrum at every learning rate, while SFT expands it at moderate learning rates; moreover, RL rotates the singular subspaces much faster than SFT at small learning rates. Interpolating between SFT and RL one ingredient at a time, we pinpoint group-mean baseline subtraction as the source of both contrasts. A quadratic multi-index model updated via LoRA unveils the underlying mechanism: group-mean baseline subtraction tilts the balance between two competing forces, coherent fitting and gradient noise, toward spectral concentration and faster subspace rotation, while forcing the risk-favorable learning rate to be low. Guided by these dynamics, we tailor LoRA updates to each stage: in SFT, we flatten the spectrum of the full update to spread adaptation across singular directions, whereas in RL, we flatten the part of the update outside the current LoRA increment span to promote subspace rotation. Experiments on mathematical reasoning tasks across multiple models show that the respective configurations for SFT and RL yield the best performance among the compared methods in most evaluated settings.

articles.title: T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of redundancy: many visual tokens are spatially irrelevant, while attention over the remaining tokens is often misallocated. Based on this observation, we propose T3R, a Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement framework. In the first stage, segmentation-guided token pruning removes irrelevant visual patches to reduce computation and eliminate distracting context. In the second stage, saliency-guided attention biasing reallocates attention toward action-critical visual regions and language instructions within the retained tokens. Together, pruning produces a cleaner candidate set, while attention biasing further emphasizes the most decision-relevant evidence, yielding a better accuracy-efficiency frontier than either stage alone. On LIBERO-Spatial, T3R removes 85% of scene-camera visual tokens while essentially matching the unpruned success rate, and improves success by up to 7 percentage points under out-of-distribution object-placement perturbations. The timing comparison attributes 7.8 ms per inference call to pruning and attention-bias application. As input resolution increases, LLM-forward profiling shows up to a 3.3x speedup over the unpruned baseline. Evaluations across LIBERO, SIMPLER, and RoboTwin with three VLA backbones show the strongest accuracy-efficiency benefits in multi-camera settings. These results demonstrate that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.

articles.title: The Gold Rush in AI4Math, II: What are signatures of AI-assisted Proofs?
articles.content: The growing use of AI in mathematics raises a question: can we detect AI involvement in proofs, separately from AI assistance with writing? Historical arXiv papers, recent papers disclosing substantive AI use, and manuscripts released by OpenAI provide a rich empirical basis for studying this question. However, several challenges remain: lack of matched case-control pairs; potential incompleteness of disclosure; and lack of ready-to-use features designed to capture signals of AI involvement in proofs.   To address these challenges, we construct five cohorts comprising 8,281 papers by combining existing manuscripts with those we produced using generative AI. These cohorts span different levels of AI involvement and include matched pairs of papers addressing the same research problems. We then introduce ProofTrace, a framework that represents each paper as a graph of immediate proof support (GIPS) and extracts interpretable features of mathematical organization.   Our study yields three discoveries. First, principal-component projections of our features reveal a qualitative gradient of AI involvement, where AI-reworded papers remain close to human papers, the two AI-generated cohorts depart in broadly shared directions, and papers disclosing substantive AI use occupy intermediate positions which shifts toward AI-generated cohorts over time. Second, we identify recurring signatures of AI-generated proofs, such as fewer externally cited results, greater reliance on intermediate conclusions, and altered graph connectivity; many of these signatures persist under controls for research field, manuscript length, or graph size. Finally, in a separate detection experiment, ProofTrace distinguishes human-written papers from those disclosing substantive AI use. Its performance remains stable under AI rewording, whereas the performance of state-of-the-art text-based detectors declines sharply.

articles.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
articles.content: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees, but in time-dependent settings common to physics and engineering, these guarantees can break down, leading to systematic undercoverage. We study this problem in the context of surrogate models for time-dependent physical systems described by partial differential equations. We prove that in a function space setting, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. We further show that in discretized settings, the total variation distance between distributions often saturates exponentially fast with the grid resolution, mandating restrictions on the spatial discretization to ensure coverage. Finally, for certain settings, we show how to use principled weighted conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample coverage guarantees over growing time horizons.

articles.title: 91% ≈ 0%？谷歌最新研究，戳破工程 Agent 的高正确率泡沫
articles.content: 41.3% 的设计项跨过安全门槛，复杂工程仍困于约束耦合。    作者丨郑佳美 岑   峰    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       在工程世界里，91% 的正确，有时和 0% 的交付能力没有区别。一条电缆桥架在机房顶部穿过消防管线，就能让几十页正确的计算书失去交付价值。载流量算对了，电压降符合要求，设备选型也有依据，但进入三维空间后，几套系统争夺同一段净空，工程师只能退回方案。AI Agent 能快速完成局部计算，工程项目却不会按计算题的边界运转：一处调整牵动另一处，刚核验过的结果也可能随修订失效。Google 与 Mercor 近日发布的 Physical-Engineering's Last Exam（PLE），以 85 项机械、电气、土木与结构工程任务量化了这种落差。在 56 项隐藏测试中，Claude Opus 5.5 搭配 Claude Code 得分 48.3%，而在共同创作任务中，它平均满足 91% 的单项约束，只有 41.3% 的交付设计项满足全部硬性安全与可行性要求。更棘手的是，剩下的 9% 往往无法靠继续提高模型的计算能力解决。因为工程设计中的要求彼此关联，解决一个问题，可能又会产生新的问题。PLE 的技术设计恰好揭示了这一困境：当局部能力已经足够强，工程 Agent 究竟还缺少什么？01工程 Agent 正在遭遇可行域瓶颈此前很多 Agent 评测采用逐项累积分数的方式，只要完成更多要求，就能取得更高评价。这适合衡量知识理解和单点执行能力，却会掩盖工程设计中的一类关键失败：模型可能满足了绝大多数要求，但剩下一条恰好决定方案能否投入使用。PLE 在 41 项人机共同创作任务中，将工程约束与设计优化放进同一套评价体系。其中 37 项采用约束评分，在统一评分机制下，40% 的评分空间取决于单项检查通过比例，另外 60% 则与成本或性能优化有关。不过，优化部分存在一个前提：全部硬性安全与可行性约束必须通过。研究团队将其称为硬约束门控（Hard-Constraint Gating）。这个机制有一处关键设计。即使某个方案能够显著降低材料费用，只要违反了一项硬约束，就无法获得成本优化部分的分数。系统仍然记录它已经完成的检查，但不会允许经济收益抵消工程缺陷。PLE 同时设置了合规但未经充分优化的基线方案，以及合规成本的下界。前者用于判断 Agent 是否产生了实际优化收益，后者则为成本改善提供衡量尺度。这样，模型既不能通过选用过量设备轻松满足规范，也无法靠牺牲可行性获得漂亮的成本数字。这种评分方式让一个长期存在的问题变得清晰：工程设计中的优化空间受到约束限制，并且约束之间往往存在联系。例如，在冷却系统设计中，管径决定水力阻力，水力阻力影响水泵工作点，而实际流量又决定换热能力。Agent 如果只根据材料成本缩小管径，后续可能需要更高扬程的水泵，原本节省的费用反而转移到设备和运行能耗上。工程上把所有约束同时成立的设计范围称为可行域。它包含连续变化的参数，也受到设备型号、标准尺寸等离散条件限制。模型每修改一个变量，其他参数能够选择的范围便可能发生变化。这给 Agent 带来一种与普通推理不同的要求。生成候选方案之后，还需要判断当前哪些条件已经接近允许边界，以及下一次修改会影响哪些约束。工程优化中，这些限制进一步调整空间的条件通常被称为活跃约束。PLE 没有直接为 Agent 提供可行域搜索算法，但硬约束门控让这种能力缺口可以被测量。91% 的单项约束满足比例说明，模型已经能够处理大部分局部要求，剩余困难集中在多个条件共同成立，以及满足条件后继续优化。而当设计从单次求解进入长时间、多轮修改时，问题还会继续扩大：此前满足的约束，未必在下一轮操作后仍然有效。02长流程能力正在变成状态一致性问题PLE 的任务环境没有将设计条件整理成一份完整说明。85 项任务累计包含 51

articles.title: 0.016% 的 Astra 微创手术，治好了 Qwen 的 3 万 Token 死循环
articles.content: 当「读懂权重」和「改写权重」被同一个模型打通，「AI 改进 AI」就多了一条不经过梯度下降的短路通道，模型维护与模型能力放大之间的边界开始模糊。    作者丨郑佳美    编辑丨岑   峰                                                                                                       一个模型做数学题，写了 3 万多个 Token，仍然在重复相似的推理过程，最后连答案也交不出来。碰到这种情况，通常会调整训练数据、优化推理策略，或者重新微调模型。但 MIT CSAIL 最近尝试了一种更直接的办法：让 GPT-6 Astra 检查 Qwen3.5-0.8B 的内部权重，找出问题发生的位置，再直接修改参数。结果，Astra 只改动了约 0.016% 的权重，就让 Qwen 的 MATH-500 成绩从 7.9% 提升到 48.1%，接近原来的 6 倍。这项研究真正的信号，不是“0.016% 权重换 6 倍成绩”这个数字，而是它把机制可解释性的输出从“解释”变成了“可执行的编辑指令”，让AI有了改造另一个AI的“抓手”。更有意思的是，同一组实验中，Astra 还能只看参数认出神经网络学过什么游戏、哪种语言，甚至从零写出一套网络权重，让它直接学会玩游戏。研究者把这种能力称为 Weight-Space Programming，即权重空间编程。它背后有一个很有意思的技术变化：当神经网络里的参数能够被还原成具体的计算过程，LLM 就有机会像修改代码一样，直接改写模型内部的功能。这件事如何实现，要从 Astra 阅读权重的方式说起。01只给一堆数字，Astra 怎么知道网络学会了什么？研究者先做了一个猜游戏的实验。他们分别训练了 4 个神经网络，让它们学会 Breakout、Pong、Pac-Man 和 Freeway。为了避免通过网络大小猜答案，4 个模型采用完全相同的架构，每个包含 17253 个参数，输入都是 10×10 的游戏网格，输出对应 5 种动作。雷峰网训练结束后，研究者只把权重交给 Astra，不告诉游戏名称，也不允许运行网络。Astra 却认出了全部 4 款游戏。它利用的是训练留在参数里的痕迹。例如 Breakout 的球拍始终沿屏幕底部移动，网络输入层中负责读取玩家位置的权重，就会集中在网格下沿。再结合输出层对左右动作的响应，Astra 便能判断网络正在控制什么。不过，游戏网络有一个便利条件：输入位置有明确的物理含义。大型语言模型的隐藏维度没有这样的标签，某个参数很大，并不能直接说明它代表什么。为了检验 Astra 能否理解更复杂的结构，研究者训练了 3 个约 720 万参数的字符级 Transformer，分别学习 Python、罗马字日语和英语。随后移除输入 Embedding 和输出层，只留下中间的 4 个 Transformer Block。这样一来，Astra 无法知道隐藏维度对应哪些字符，也不能运行模型观察输出，只能分析内部矩阵之间的关系。它找到的突破口是 Induction Head，也就是 Transformer 中帮助模型复制历史文本的一类 Attention Head。例如，前文已经出现过 total，后文再次出现 tot，模型可以找到之前相同的片段，接着生成 al。这个操作看似简单，内部却需要完成两件事：先定位历史中的重复片段，再把它后面的字符信息带到当前位置。在 Transformer 中，QK 电路负责决定读取历史中的哪个位置，OV 电路负责决定读取的信息怎样写回隐藏状态。而一次完整的复制操作，往往需要不同 Attention Head 配合：前面的 Head 提供字符位置关系，后面的 Head 利用这些信息寻找匹配片段。Astra 沿着信息传递路径分析不同 Head 的矩阵乘积，寻找能够完成这种配合的结构。结果，它在 Python 模型中找到了 3 个 copying head，在另外两个模型中各找到 1 个，随后通过实际运行网络得

articles.title: 当10万个智能体已在运行，安全防线到底在哪？｜CNCC 2026专家激辩智能体安全挑战
articles.content: 2026年，智能体从概念走向了生产系统。蚂蚁集团3万多名员工背后，已有10万余个智能体在运行。华为内部同样部署了成千上万个智能体，覆盖客服、办公、运维、研发各条业务线。放眼更广的产业图景，个人助手、AI for Science、网络安全自动化攻防、企业级工作流编排，智能体正在逐步接管人类过去亲力亲为的工作。Gartner将智能体列入了2027年十大战略技术，安全圈里，非人类身份（NHI）成了RSAC大会上的新赛道。中国这边，国标、强标、最高法司法意见、三部委规范文件在今年密集出台，政策端的紧迫感与产业端的狂飙几乎同步。10月22日，成都，在CNCC 2026”智能体的安全问题”专题论坛上，于锐、徐恪、胡侠、韦韬、肖亚军五位嘉宾齐聚一堂，分别从国家标准制定、高校AI安全研究、企业安全最后一道防线等角度，做出了各自的解读。01 中国开始给智能体发“身份证”安全的第一步是搞清楚“它是谁”。但智能体能自主行动、跨平台迁移、在无人监督下链式决策和调用工具，传统的人类身份认证方式显然并不适用。CCF计算机安全专委会副主任委员于锐介绍，“中国在这方面的进展可以概括为三句话：国标引领、行业细化、企业落地。”今年5月出台的GB/T 185系列标准覆盖了智能体安全治理的全生命周期，两个核心要求是授予每个智能体唯一的身份标识，以及实施统一的身份管理。编码方式采用OID，树形分层结构，一码一主体，永不重复。“跟我们人一样，也给智能体发了一个身份号码。”于锐表示。另一个正在制定的强制性标准是《智能体应用安全基本条件》，该标准一旦发布，没有身份和标识的智能体将无法上线应用。而身份只是最表层的一环，于锐将智能体的身份拆为三层：第一层是产品身份，包含智能体的ID、代码指纹和版本号，用于回答“这是哪个智能体”；第二层是运行时身份，校验其运行环境、设备信息和调用来源，反映“它此刻在做什么”；第三层是责任主体，通过实名认证和企业认定，解决的是“出了事找谁”。“不是授一次权就让它一直做下去，按任务给最低授权，任务完成就收回权限。”于锐强调。技术实现层面，认证走OAuth/OIDC，授权走OAuth，凭证参考JWT格式。但无论走哪条技术路线，最终都绕不开一个关键问题：信任的锚点。关于这一点，于锐介绍了他们正在建设的国家网络可信身份公共服务平台。国标的OID、W3C的DID、IETF基于DNS的方案，信任锚点都落在实名认证上。“这个国家平台是新型数字基础设施，主要是给公民签发线上的网号网证，就是你线上的身份标识和可验证凭证。”于锐介绍，平台的实施管理办法今年7月正式发布，目前已达到每秒15万次的服务能力，接入了900多个机构，下载申领量突破6000万。“目的就是形成一个数字空间的信任根，来支撑国标185的落地。”身份解决了“智能体是谁”的问题，但在责任归属上，由于智能体不是人，没有法律资格无法自己承担责任，这一点国内外并无分歧。对此，今年9月，最高人民法院发布了《关于审理涉人工智能纠纷案件的意见》，按控制力、场景和获利划分责任：一般场景适用过错责任，开发者和使用者承担风控告知和复核义务；具身智能场景适用产品责任，机器人造成伤害，制造商承担无过错责任；涉及个人信息的场景实行过错推定，由运营方自证合规。02 旧安全架构无法抵挡新攻击标准和法规在加速推进，但技术侧的问题更为棘手。“中文里‘安全’是两个字，英文里是safety、security、reliability、privacy、stability、trustworthiness，无数概念混在其中。AI这一轮爆发之后，攻防天平已经严重失衡。”对于智能体安全问题现状，蚂蚁集团副总裁兼首席技术安全官、蚂蚁密算科技有限公司董事长韦韬感慨道。韦韬透露，就在大会前两天，一家知名的数据库公司全面爆雷，紧随其后，PHP和NodeJS接连曝出高危漏洞。“大模型领域广泛使用的LiteLLM网关被投毒，攻击者在全面利用AI提升攻击效率。”防守方的处境则更加被动，AI编程导致代码产出速度暴涨，许多公司一个月的漏洞产出量已经相当于过去一年，修复速度始终无法跟上。“大家非常熟悉的DAC、MAC、贝尔-拉帕杜拉这些访问控制模型，是在六七十年代主机时代起来的，在局域网时代完善的。到了云时代，整个链条持续扩大，主体爆炸、客体爆炸、链条爆炸，访问控制模型已经严重失衡了。”韦韬指出，AI攻击能力的爆发式提升让各家的欠债集中暴露。与此同时，智能体带来的不只是旧问题的放大，还有全新的结构性隐患。韦韬将矛头指向了更底层的根源：自然语言本身就不适合作为安全载体。“今天大家造智能体的习惯是自然语言加Guardrails，智能部分靠自然语言，过程部分靠Guardrails。但自然语言是一个非常糟糕的载体，含混，条件描述讲不清楚，逻辑控制的边界也讲不清楚，表达里到处是go
